ingredients.note: use chicken broth if you don't need it vegetarian

instructions: Blend the bell peppers, tomatoes, chopped onion, Scotch bonnet, garlic and ginger until smooth. Simmer this pepper base in a saucepan over medium heat for 10 minutes, stirring now and then, until it thickens and loses its raw smell.
Heat the oil in a heavy Dutch oven over medium heat. Fry the sliced onion for 4 minutes until soft, then stir in the tomato paste and fry it for 3 to 4 minutes until it darkens to a brick red.
Add the reduced pepper base, curry powder, thyme, bay leaves and salt. Fry the sauce for 5 minutes, stirring, until oil starts to pool on the surface.
Stir in the rinsed rice and broth, bring to a boil, then turn the heat to the lowest setting. Cover with a sheet of foil and then the lid to trap the steam.

Cook for 25 to 30 minutes without stirring, until the rice is tender and the liquid is absorbed. If the rice is still firm, sprinkle in 1/4 cup water and cook 5 minutes more; a little toasty crust on the bottom is prized.
Remove the bay leaves, fluff with a fork and adjust the salt. Serve with fried plantains, chicken or a simple salad.

recipes.title: Groundnut Stew with Chicken and Sweet Potatoes
recipes.summary: West African peanut stew: chicken and sweet potato simmered in a rich tomato and peanut sauce with spinach. Mild to medium heat; drop the Scotch bonnet for kids.

ingredients.name: chicken thighs
ingredients.note: boneless, skinless, cut into large chunks

ingredients.name: sweet potatoes
ingredients.note: peeled and cut into 1-inch cubes (about 1 1/2 lb)

ingredients.name: scotch bonnet pepper
ingredients.note: left whole and pricked for gentle heat; find it at Caribbean or African grocers, or some supermarkets; or use 1 habanero, or 1 jalapeño for much milder

instructions: Season the chicken with 1 tsp salt. Heat the oil in a Dutch oven over medium-high heat and brown the chicken in two batches, about 4 minutes per batch, then set aside.
Lower the heat to medium, add the onion and cook 5 minutes until soft. Stir in the garlic, ginger, smoked paprika and tomato paste and cook 2 minutes until the paste darkens.
Add the tomatoes and broth, then whisk in the peanut butter until smooth. Return the chicken, add the sweet potatoes and drop in the whole pricked Scotch bonnet.
Bring to a boil, then simmer partly covered for 25 to 30 minutes, stirring often so the peanut sauce doesn't catch, until the sweet potatoes are tender and the sauce coats a spoon.
Fish out the Scotch bonnet (or mash it into the stew for more heat). Stir in the spinach until wilted and season with salt.
Serve over rice or with fufu, sprinkled with chopped peanuts.

recipes.title: Chicken Yassa (Senegalese Lemon-Onion Chicken)
recipes.summary: Senegal's beloved yassa: lemon-and-mustard marinated chicken browned, then braised in a mountain of soft, tangy onions. Gentle warmth; the chili is optional.

ingredients.name: scotch bonnet pepper
ingredients.note: left whole for a hint of heat; find it at Caribbean or African grocers, or some supermarkets; or use 1 habanero, or 1 jalapeño for much milder

instructions: Mix the lemon juice, mustard, garlic, salt, pepper and 1 tbsp oil in a large bowl. Add the chicken and sliced onions and toss well; marinate at least 15 minutes, or covered in the fridge up to overnight.

Lift the chicken out of the marinade and pat dry, keeping the onions and liquid. Heat 1 tbsp oil in a Dutch oven over medium-high heat and brown the chicken skin side down for 6 to 7 minutes until deep golden, then set aside.
Add the remaining oil and the onions (shake off the marinade, but keep it). Cook over medium heat, stirring often, for 15 minutes until the onions are soft, sweet and light golden.
Pour in the reserved marinade and broth, add the bay leaves and the whole Scotch bonnet if using, and nestle the chicken back in skin side up.
Cover and simmer gently for 25 minutes, adding the olives for the last 5 minutes, until the chicken is tender and at least 175°F near the bone.
Taste the onion sauce and adjust with salt or a squeeze more lemon, then serve over white rice.

recipes.title: Red-Red (Ghanaian Black-Eyed Pea Stew with Baked Plantains)
recipes.summary: Ghana's red-red: black-eyed peas in a rich tomato and palm oil sauce, served with sweet oven-baked plantains instead of fried. Mild-medium heat; skip the chili for kids.

ingredients.name: ripe plantains
ingredients.note: yellow with plenty of black spots

ingredients.name: red palm oil
ingredients.note: find it at African or Latin grocers or online; or use vegetable oil plus 1/2 tsp sweet paprika for color

ingredients.name: scotch bonnet pepper
ingredients.note: minced, seeds removed; find it at Caribbean or African grocers, or some supermarkets; or use 1 habanero, or 1 jalapeño for much milder

instructions: Heat the oven to 425°F and line a sheet pan with parchment. Peel the plantains, slice on the diagonal 1/2 inch thick, toss with the vegetable oil and a pinch of salt, and spread out in one layer.
Bake the plantains for 20 to 25 minutes, flipping halfway, until caramelized and dark golden at the edges.
Meanwhile, warm the palm oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Add the onion and cook 5 minutes until soft, then add the garlic, ginger and Scotch bonnet and cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in the tomato paste and smoked paprika and fry for 2 minutes until brick red, then add the diced tomatoes and simmer 6 to 8 minutes until thick and jammy.
Add the black-eyed peas and water, simmer 10 minutes, and lightly mash a few peas against the pan to thicken the sauce. Season with salt.
Serve the stew with the baked plantains alongside. Traditionally it is topped with gari (toasted cassava), if you can find it.

recipes.title: Suya-Spiced Chicken Skewers
recipes.summary: Nigerian street-food suya flavors on chicken: a peanut, ginger and cayenne rub, grilled until charred and served with sliced onion and tomato. Fairly hot; halve the cayenne for milder.

ingredients.name: roasted peanuts
ingredients.note: unsalted, finely ground in a food processor (stop before it turns to butter)

instructions: If using wooden skewers, soak them in water for 15 minutes. Mix the ground peanuts, paprika, cayenne, ginger, garlic powder, onion powder and crumbled bouillon cube to make the yaji (suya spice).
Toss the chicken with the oil, then with about two-thirds of the spice mix until well coated. Thread onto skewers, leaving small gaps between pieces.
Heat a grill or grill pan to medium-high and oil the grates. Grill the skewers for 10 to 12 minutes, turning every few minutes, until charred in spots and the chicken reaches 165°F.
Sprinkle the hot skewers with a little more of the remaining spice mix, keeping some at the table for anyone who wants more heat.
Pile onto a platter with the red onion, tomatoes and cucumber, and squeeze lime over just before serving.

recipes.title: Efo Riro with Shrimp (Nigerian Spinach Stew)
recipes.summary: A Yoruba-style spinach stew: spinach folded into a fried red pepper sauce with shrimp. Made approachable with frozen spinach. Medium-hot; use half the Scotch bonnet for milder.

ingredients.name: yellow onion
ingredients.note: half roughly chopped for blending, half thinly sliced

ingredients.name: scotch bonnet pepper
ingredients.note: find it at Caribbean or African grocers, or some supermarkets; or use 1 habanero, or 1 jalapeño for much milder

ingredients.name: red palm oil
ingredients.note: find it at African or Latin grocers or online; or use vegetable oil plus 1/2 tsp sweet paprika for color

ingredients.name: frozen chopped spinach
ingredients.note: thawed and squeezed very dry; or 2 lb fresh spinach, blanched and squeezed

ingredients.name: smoked paprika
ingredients.note: stands in for the smoky depth of dried fish

ingredients.name: ground crayfish
ingredients.note: find it at African grocers or online; skip if you can't find it

instructions: Blend the bell peppers, tomatoes, the chopped half onion and the Scotch bonnet until fairly smooth. Simmer in a saucepan over medium heat for 10 minutes until reduced and thick.
Warm the palm oil in a wide pot over medium heat. Add the sliced onion and garlic and cook 3 to 4 minutes until soft and fragrant.
Add the reduced pepper sauce, bouillon cube, smoked paprika and crayfish if using. Fry for 8 to 10 minutes, stirring, until the sauce darkens and the oil rises to the top.
Add the shrimp and cook 2 to 3 minutes, turning, until just pink.
Stir in the squeezed spinach, cover and cook 3 to 4 minutes until heated through; don't overcook or the spinach turns drab. Season with salt and serve with rice, pounded yam or fufu.

recipes.title: Chicken Karahi
recipes.summary: Lahore-style karahi: chicken cooked fast and hot with tomatoes, ginger, garlic, black pepper and green chilies until the sauce clings. Medium-hot; use 1 seeded chili for milder.

ingredients.name: chicken thighs
ingredients.note: boneless or bone-in, cut into 2-inch pieces

ingredients.name: ginger
ingredients.note: half grated, half cut into thin matchsticks for garnish

ingredients.name: serrano peppers
ingredients.note: slit lengthwise; use 1, seeded, for milder

ingredients.name: kashmiri chili powder
ingredients.note: or 1/2 tsp paprika plus 1/4 tsp cayenne

instructions: Heat the oil in a wok, karahi or wide skillet over high heat. Add the chicken and fry for 6 to 8 minutes, stirring, until it loses its pink color and starts to brown at the edges.
Add the garlic and grated ginger and stir-fry 1 minute. Add the tomatoes and salt, cover, and cook on medium-high for 8 minutes until the tomatoes collapse.
Uncover and use a spoon to pick out and discard any loose tomato skins if you like. Stir in the chili powder, coriander, cumin and black pepper.
Keep cooking uncovered on high, stirring and scraping, for 8 to 10 minutes until the sauce thickens, the oil separates around the edges and the chicken is cooked through.
Lower the heat, stir in the yogurt and slit serranos and cook 2 minutes more. Add the ghee if using, sprinkle with garam masala, ginger matchsticks and cilantro, and serve with naan or roti.

recipes.title: Daal Chawal (Chana Daal with Cumin Rice)
recipes.summary: Pakistan's everyday comfort plate: creamy split chickpea daal finished with a sizzling garlic and red chili tarka, over cumin rice. Mild-medium; skip the dried chilies for kids.

ingredients.name: chana dal
ingredients.note: find it at South Asian grocers; or use yellow split peas (cook 10 to 15 minutes longer)

ingredients.name: chili powder
ingredients.note: use kashmiri chili powder or paprika for milder

ingredients.name: vegetable oil
ingredients.note: or ghee, if you don't need it vegan

instructions: Rinse the chana dal and soak it in hot water while you prep, about 10 minutes. Drain, then simmer with 4 cups water, the turmeric, chili powder and 1 tsp salt, partly covered, for 40 to 45 minutes until the dal is soft and breaks when pressed; add more water if it gets too thick.
Meanwhile, put the rice, 1/2 tsp cumin seeds, 1/2 tsp salt and 2 1/4 cups water in a pot. Bring to a boil, cover and cook on the lowest heat for 15 minutes, then rest 5 minutes off the heat.
Whisk or mash the cooked dal lightly so it turns creamy but still has some texture. Stir in the chopped tomato and simmer 5 minutes.

For the tarka, heat the oil in a small skillet over medium-high heat. Fry the onion for 6 to 8 minutes until deep golden, then add the remaining cumin, the garlic and dried chilies and cook 30 to 60 seconds until the garlic is light golden.
Pour the sizzling tarka over the dal, scatter with cilantro and serve over the cumin rice with lemon wedges and a simple salad or achar on the side.

recipes.title: Aloo Keema (Spiced Ground Beef with Potatoes)
recipes.summary: A Pakistani home-cooking staple: ground beef simmered with onions, tomatoes, warm spices, potatoes and peas. Mild-medium; leave out the green chili for kids.

ingredients.name: potatoes
ingredients.note: Yukon Gold, peeled and cut into 3/4-inch cubes

instructions: Heat the oil in a deep skillet over medium-high heat and cook the onion for 6 to 7 minutes until golden at the edges.
Add the garlic and ginger and cook 1 minute, then add the beef and break it up with a spoon. Cook 5 to 6 minutes until no pink remains.
Stir in the tomatoes, salt, cumin, coriander, turmeric and chili powder. Cook 5 minutes, stirring, until the tomatoes break down and the oil starts to separate from the meat.
Add the potatoes and water, cover and simmer on medium-low for 15 minutes, stirring once or twice, until the potatoes are tender when pierced.

Stir in the peas, garam masala and serrano if using, and cook uncovered 3 to 4 minutes until the peas are hot and the mixture is thick rather than soupy. Finish with cilantro and serve with roti, naan or rice.

recipes.title: Chana Pulao (Chickpea Rice with Whole Spices)
recipes.summary: Fragrant basmati cooked in a light onion stock with chickpeas and whole spices: a classic Pakistani one-pot rice. Gently spiced, not hot; serve with raita for dairy-eaters.

ingredients.name: basmati rice
ingredients.note: rinsed, then soaked 20 minutes and drained

ingredients.name: green cardamom pods
ingredients.note: lightly crushed; find them in the spice aisle or South Asian grocers

instructions: Heat the oil in a heavy pot over medium heat. Add the onion and cook, stirring, for 10 to 12 minutes until evenly deep golden brown; this color gives the pulao its flavor.
Add the cumin, cinnamon, cardamom, cloves, peppercorns and bay leaves and stir for 30 seconds until fragrant. Add the garlic, ginger and tomato and cook 3 minutes until the tomato softens.
Add the chickpeas, broth and salt and bring to a rolling boil. Taste the liquid: it should be a little saltier than you'd like soup.
Gently stir in the drained rice, return to a boil and cook uncovered on medium-high for 3 to 4 minutes until the water drops just below the surface of the rice and little holes appear.
Cover tightly, turn the heat to the lowest setting and cook 12 minutes. Turn off the heat and rest, covered, for 5 minutes.
Fluff gently with a fork, scatter with cilantro and serve with raita or a cucumber-tomato salad.

recipes.title: Weeknight Chicken Biryani
recipes.summary: A streamlined Pakistani-style chicken biryani: spiced yogurt chicken layered with par-boiled basmati, fried onions and mint, then steamed. Medium heat; use 1 chili for milder.

ingredients.name: biryani masala
ingredients.note: find it in the international aisle or South Asian grocers; or use 2 tbsp garam masala plus 1 tsp chili powder

ingredients.name: salt
ingredients.note: divided, plus more for the rice water

ingredients.name: potatoes
ingredients.note: small Yukon Gold, peeled and halved; a Karachi favorite

ingredients.name: whole milk
ingredients.note: warmed, with a pinch of saffron or 2 drops yellow food coloring

instructions: Mix the chicken with the yogurt, biryani masala, garlic, ginger and 1 1/2 tsp salt and set aside while you fry the onions.
Heat the oil in a Dutch oven over medium-high heat and fry the onions, stirring often, for 12 to 15 minutes until deep golden brown. Lift out half for layering.

Add the tomatoes and serranos to the pot and cook 4 minutes until soft. Add the chicken and its marinade and the potatoes if using, then cover and simmer on medium-low for 20 minutes, stirring once, until the chicken is cooked and the sauce is thick.
Meanwhile, bring a large pot of water to a boil with 2 tbsp salt. Add the drained rice and boil for 5 to 6 minutes until it is about 70% cooked, still firm in the center, then drain.

Scatter half the mint, cilantro and reserved onions over the chicken, sprinkle with lemon juice, then spread the rice on top. Top with the remaining herbs and onions and drizzle over the saffron milk if using.

Cover tightly with foil and the lid and cook on the lowest heat for 15 to 18 minutes until the rice is tender and steaming. Rest 5 minutes, then scoop from the bottom so everyone gets chicken and rice. Serve with raita.

recipes.title: Oven-Baked Seekh Kebabs
recipes.summary: Pakistani BBQ-style seekh kebabs, shaped on skewers and broiled: juicy ground beef with onion, ginger, green chili and herbs. Medium heat; seed the chilies for milder.

ingredients.name: serrano peppers
ingredients.note: finely minced; seed them for milder

instructions: Heat the broiler with a rack about 6 inches below it and line a sheet pan with foil. If using wooden skewers, soak 8 of them in water.

Put the beef, squeezed onion, garlic, ginger, serranos, cilantro, mint, cumin, coriander, garam masala, chili flakes and salt in a bowl. Knead firmly with your hands for 2 to 3 minutes until the mixture turns sticky; this keeps the kebabs on the skewers.
With wet hands, divide into 8 portions and squeeze each one into a long, even sausage around a skewer, about 1 inch thick. Chill 10 minutes if they feel soft.
Lay the skewers on the pan, brush with oil and broil for 10 to 12 minutes, turning every 4 minutes, until browned and charred in spots and 160°F inside.
Rest 2 minutes, then serve with onion rings, lemon wedges, naan and mint chutney or yogurt sauce.

recipes.title: New Orleans Red Beans and Rice
recipes.summary: New Orleans red beans simmered with the trinity, andouille and a ham hock until creamy, served over rice. A cheap, hands-off pot that tastes better the next day; mild, with hot sauce at the table.

ingredients.name: dried red kidney beans
ingredients.note: Camellia brand if you can find it (it's the New Orleans standard); small red beans also work and cook a little faster.

ingredients.name: andouille sausage
ingredients.note: sliced into 1/4-inch coins; any smoked pork sausage works

ingredients.name: smoked ham hock
ingredients.note: about 1 lb; or a meaty ham bone, 8 oz diced smoked ham or tasso, or pickled pork (pickle meat) from a Louisiana market

ingredients.name: cayenne pepper
ingredients.note: up to 1/2 tsp if you like more heat

ingredients.name: salt
ingredients.note: add at the end, to taste; sausage and ham are salty

ingredients.name: louisiana hot sauce
ingredients.note: Crystal or Tabasco, for the table; any vinegary hot sauce works

instructions: The night before, cover the beans with cold water by 3 inches and soak. Next day, drain and rinse them, picking out any stones or shriveled beans.

Heat the oil in a large heavy pot or Dutch oven over medium heat. Brown the andouille 5 to 6 minutes, stirring, until the edges are dark and some fat has rendered. Scoop it out and set aside, leaving the fat in the pot.
Add the onion, bell pepper and celery and cook 8 to 10 minutes, scraping up the browned bits, until soft and the onion is turning golden. Stir in the garlic for the last minute.
Add the beans, ham hock if using, bay leaves, thyme, cayenne, black pepper and 10 cups of water. Bring to a boil, then lower to a gentle simmer, partly covered.
Simmer about 2 hours, stirring every 20 minutes and scraping the bottom so nothing sticks. Add hot water a cup at a time if the beans peek above the liquid.

When the beans are completely tender, return the sausage. Pull out the ham hock, shred any meat off the bone and stir it back in. Mash about a cup of beans against the side of the pot with your spoon and simmer uncovered another 30 to 45 minutes, until the liquid is thick, creamy and gravy-like.
Meanwhile cook the rice. Fish out the bay leaves, taste the beans and add salt only now. Serve the beans over rice with green onions on top and hot sauce on the side.

recipes.title: Shrimp Étouffée
recipes.summary: Cajun-style shrimp smothered in a buttery blond-roux gravy with the trinity and shell stock, no tomato, over rice. A weeknight-doable hour; mildly spicy.

ingredients.name: shrimp
ingredients.note: large (26 to 30 per lb), shell-on; peel and devein, keeping the shells. Frozen Louisiana crawfish tails (seafood case) are the classic swap: they're already cooked, so don't rinse off the yellow fat and just heat them through 2 to 3 minutes.

ingredients.name: cajun seasoning
ingredients.note: salt-based blend like Tony Chachere's or Slap Ya Mama; if yours is salt-free, add 1 tsp salt

ingredients.name: green onions
ingredients.note: sliced, whites and greens kept separate

ingredients.name: louisiana hot sauce
ingredients.note: Crystal or Tabasco, for the table; any vinegary hot sauce works

instructions: Put the shrimp shells (and heads, if you bought head-on) in a saucepan with 4 cups of water. Bring to a boil and simmer 15 minutes while you chop, then strain; you want about 3 cups. Use boxed seafood stock or clam juice cut with water if you're short on time.
Season the peeled shrimp with 1/2 tsp of the Cajun seasoning and keep them in the fridge. Start the rice.

Melt the butter in a large heavy skillet or Dutch oven over medium heat. Whisk in the flour and cook, stirring constantly, 6 to 8 minutes until it smells nutty and is the color of peanut butter. Don't walk away; if you see black specks, start over.

Add the onion, bell pepper, celery and green-onion whites all at once (this cools the roux). Cook 8 minutes, stirring, until soft. Add the garlic, the rest of the Cajun seasoning, paprika, cayenne and thyme and stir 1 minute.

Slowly stir in 2 1/2 cups of the warm stock, a ladle at a time, until smooth. Add the bay leaves and simmer gently, uncovered, 10 to 15 minutes, until it coats a spoon like gravy. Thin with more stock if it gets too thick.
Stir in the shrimp and cook 3 to 4 minutes, just until they turn pink and curl into a C. Turn off the heat and stir in the lemon juice, green-onion tops and parsley.
Remove the bay leaves, taste and add salt or more cayenne as needed. Spoon over rice and pass the hot sauce.

recipes.title: Chicken Tagine with Preserved Lemon and Olives
recipes.summary: Moroccan djaj mqualli: chicken braised with grated onion, ginger, saffron and turmeric until the sauce turns silky, then finished with salty preserved lemon and green olives. Not spicy.

ingredients.name: chicken thighs
ingredients.note: bone-in (about 8); pull off the skin if you like a less oily sauce, or use a whole chicken cut into pieces

ingredients.name: yellow onions
ingredients.note: large, coarsely grated on a box grater

ingredients.name: saffron threads
ingredients.note: crumbled into 2 tbsp warm water; sold in small jars in the spice aisle; skip it and add another 1/2 tsp turmeric if you must

ingredients.name: salt
ingredients.note: go easy: the lemon and olives bring plenty

ingredients.name: fresh cilantro
ingredients.note: tied with the parsley into a bundle

ingredients.name: preserved lemon
ingredients.note: jarred, from Middle Eastern grocers, Whole Foods or the olive bar; or simmer strips of zest from 1 lemon with 1 tsp salt and 2 tbsp lemon juice for 5 minutes

ingredients.name: green olives
ingredients.note: cracked green, picholine or Castelvetrano; red-brown Moroccan olives are traditional too; not Kalamata

instructions: In a Dutch oven or tagine, stir the chicken with the garlic, ginger, turmeric, saffron and its water, pepper, salt and olive oil until every piece is yellow. If you have time, leave it 30 minutes or overnight in the fridge.

Add the grated onions and set the pot over medium heat. Cook, turning the chicken now and then, for about 10 minutes, until the onions soften and smell sweet and the chicken firms up; it should not brown.
Pour in the water, tuck the herb bundle among the chicken, cover and cook at a gentle simmer for 45 minutes, turning the pieces halfway, until the meat is tender and pulls easily from the bone.

Meanwhile, quarter the preserved lemon, scrape out and discard the pulp and seeds, and cut the rind into strips. Rinse the olives; if they taste very salty, simmer them in fresh water for 3 minutes and drain.

Lift out and discard the herb bundle. Scatter the lemon rind and olives over the chicken and simmer uncovered for 10 to 15 minutes, spooning the sauce over, until the onions have melted into a thick, glossy sauce that coats a spoon. If it is still thin, lift the chicken onto a plate, boil the sauce hard for a few minutes, then return the chicken. Add a splash of water if it catches.
Taste before adding any salt, add the lemon juice if you like it sharper, and serve straight from the pot with crusty bread or Moroccan khobz for mopping. It tastes even better reheated the next day.

recipes.title: Tunisian Lablabi (Garlicky Chickpea Soup over Bread)
recipes.summary: Tunisia's street-cart breakfast: cumin and garlic chickpea broth ladled over torn day-old bread, topped with a jammy egg, harissa, capers and good olive oil. Medium heat; stir in harissa to taste.

ingredients.name: canned chickpeas
ingredients.note: 15 oz each; drain one can and keep the liquid from the other

ingredients.name: garlic
ingredients.note: 4 smashed for the pot, 2 crushed to a paste with a pinch of salt

ingredients.name: harissa
ingredients.note: Tunisian-style in a tube or jar from the international aisle or Middle Eastern grocers; or use sambal oelek with a pinch each of ground caraway and coriander

ingredients.name: olive oil
ingredients.note: a fruity extra-virgin one, for drizzling

ingredients.name: day-old crusty bread
ingredients.note: torn into bite-size pieces, about half a baguette; stale is better than fresh

instructions: Put the chickpeas (one can drained, one with its liquid), water, the 4 smashed garlic cloves, cumin and salt in a pot. Bring to a boil, then simmer for 15 to 20 minutes, until the chickpeas are very soft and the broth tastes of garlic and cumin.

While it simmers, lower the eggs into a small pot of boiling water and cook 6 1/2 minutes for jammy yolks. Cool them in cold water, peel and halve. (Many Tunis carts instead crack a raw egg into each bowl just before the hot broth goes in and stir it through; do that only if you're happy with a barely set egg.)
Stir the crushed garlic paste and 1 tbsp of the harissa into the soup and taste for salt. Mash a few chickpeas against the side of the pot if you want a thicker broth.
Divide the torn bread among 4 deep bowls and ladle the hot broth and chickpeas over it, letting the bread soak for a minute so it turns soft and spoonable.

Top each bowl with a halved egg, a little dab of the remaining harissa, a pinch of cumin, a few capers and a generous drizzle of olive oil. Serve with lemon wedges and let everyone stir it all together; add more harissa at the table for more heat.

recipes.title: Tortilla Española (Potato and Onion Omelette)
recipes.summary: Spain's thick potato omelette: potatoes and onion slowly poached in olive oil, then set in beaten eggs until just creamy inside. Cheap, good warm or at room temperature, and great for next-day lunches.

ingredients.name: yukon gold potatoes
ingredients.note: peeled, quartered lengthwise and sliced about 1/8 inch thick; russets also work

ingredients.name: olive oil
ingredients.note: plain olive oil is fine (many Spanish homes use extra-virgin); you'll pour most of it off and can strain and reuse it

instructions: Heat the oil in a 10-inch nonstick skillet over medium heat until a potato slice sizzles gently. Add the potatoes and onion with 1 teaspoon of the salt; most of them should sit in the oil; any that poke out will cook as you turn them.

Cook at a gentle bubble, turning every few minutes with a spatula, for 20 to 25 minutes, until the potatoes are completely tender and break when pressed but have barely browned. Turn the heat down if they start to color fast.
Meanwhile, beat the eggs with the remaining 1/2 teaspoon salt in a large bowl until uniform.

Set a colander over a heatproof bowl and drain the potatoes and onion, keeping the oil. While still hot, stir them into the eggs, pressing a few pieces to break them up, and let it sit 5 to 10 minutes so the potatoes soak up some egg.

Wipe out the skillet, add 2 tablespoons of the reserved oil and heat over medium-high until shimmering. Pour in the egg mixture, spread it level, and lower the heat to medium-low. Shake the pan and run a spatula around the edge now and then for 5 to 6 minutes, until the edges are set and the bottom is golden but the top is still loose.

Put a flat plate or lid bigger than the pan upside down over the skillet. Holding them together firmly (use oven mitts), flip in one confident move so the tortilla lands on the plate, then slide it back into the pan, uncooked side down. Tuck the edges under with the spatula to round them.

Cook 2 to 4 minutes more: 2 for a soft, juicy center the way most Spanish homes like it, 4 if you want it set all the way through. Slide onto a plate and rest at least 10 minutes before cutting into wedges or small squares. Refrigerate leftovers up to 3 days.

recipes.title: Gazpacho Andaluz
recipes.summary: Andalusia's chilled blended soup of ripe tomatoes, cucumber, green pepper, garlic, olive oil and sherry vinegar. No stove at all; the thing to make with summer tomatoes on a hot day.

ingredients.name: tomatoes
ingredients.note: very ripe, cored and roughly chopped; Roma or on-the-vine work, and peak summer tomatoes make all the difference

ingredients.name: cucumber
ingredients.note: English cucumber, peeled and chopped, or 2 small Persian cucumbers

ingredients.name: cubanelle pepper
ingredients.note: seeded and chopped; stands in for the Spanish Italian-style green frying pepper, or use half a green bell pepper

ingredients.name: garlic
ingredients.note: peeled; use half if your garlic is strong

ingredients.name: extra-virgin olive oil
ingredients.note: Spanish if you can find it

ingredients.name: sherry vinegar
ingredients.note: in the vinegar aisle; or red wine vinegar

ingredients.name: crusty bread
ingredients.note: a thick slice of day-old white bread, crust removed, soaked in water and squeezed; makes it creamier. Leave it out for a gluten-free gazpacho

ingredients.name: red onion
ingredients.note: chopped; some families add it, others never do

instructions: Put the tomatoes, cucumber, pepper, garlic, salt, vinegar and the soaked bread and onion if using in a blender. Blend on high for 1 to 2 minutes until completely smooth.
With the blender running, pour in the olive oil in a thin stream. The soup will turn from red to a paler orange-pink and look creamy; that means it's emulsified.

For a silky texture, press it through a fine sieve with the back of a ladle, or skip this if you don't mind a little texture. Stir in cold water until it's as thin as you like; it should pour easily but not be watery.
Taste and adjust with more salt or a splash of vinegar; it should taste bright and well seasoned, because cold dulls flavor.

Cover and refrigerate at least 2 hours, until very cold. Stir before serving in glasses, or in bowls topped with finely diced cucumber, pepper and a drizzle of olive oil. It keeps 3 days in the fridge.

recipes.title: Spanish Chicken and Chorizo Rice, Paella-Style
recipes.summary: Browned chicken thighs, Spanish chorizo, saffron and pimentón cooked unstirred in one wide pan until the bottom turns crisp. It's cooked the paella way, but with chorizo it's a Spanish home arroz, not a Valencian paella.

ingredients.name: spanish chorizo
ingredients.note: the dry, cured kind sold whole near the deli cheeses, not fresh Mexican chorizo; sliced into thin half-moons. Most Spanish brands are gluten-free, but check the label

ingredients.name: red bell pepper
ingredients.note: seeded and cut into thin strips

ingredients.name: tomato
ingredients.note: large, halved and grated on a box grater, skin discarded; or 1/2 cup canned crushed tomatoes

ingredients.name: smoked paprika
ingredients.note: sweet smoked Spanish pimentón (pimentón de la Vera dulce), sold in small tins in the spice aisle; regular sweet paprika also works

ingredients.name: saffron threads
ingredients.note: loosely packed, a good pinch; in the spice aisle or at Latin grocers

ingredients.name: bomba rice
ingredients.note: Spanish short-grain paella rice, online or at specialty stores; or Calasparra, or a medium-grain rice like Goya (see the steps for less broth)

ingredients.name: lemon
ingredients.note: cut into wedges, for serving; not done in Valencia, but some people like it

instructions: Crumble the saffron into the hot broth and let it steep while you cook. Season the chicken with half the salt.

Heat the oil in a 12-inch skillet or 14-inch paella pan over medium-high. Brown the chicken in one layer, turning, for 7 to 8 minutes until golden on all sides. Add the chorizo and cook 1 to 2 minutes until it releases its red oil.

Push the meat to the edges, add the onion and pepper to the center and cook, stirring, for 6 to 8 minutes until soft and starting to brown. Add the garlic for 30 seconds, then the grated tomato, and cook 4 to 5 minutes until it darkens and thickens to a jammy paste.
Lower the heat, stir in the paprika for a few seconds (it burns fast), then add the rice and stir for 1 minute so every grain is coated in the oil.

Pour in the hot saffron broth and the remaining salt. Taste the liquid: it should be pleasantly salty. Stir once to spread the rice evenly across the pan, bring to a lively boil, and from now on do not stir. If using medium-grain rice instead of bomba, use 3 3/4 cups broth.

Boil over medium-high for 8 to 10 minutes, rotating the pan over the burner every couple of minutes so it cooks evenly, until the rice peeks through the surface of the liquid. Scatter the peas over the top if using.

Turn the heat to low and cook 8 to 10 minutes more, until the liquid is absorbed and the rice is tender with a slight bite. If it dries before the rice is done, sprinkle on a few tablespoons of hot water.

For the socarrat, raise the heat to medium-high for 1 to 2 minutes until you hear crackling and smell toasting rice (not burning). Take it off the heat, cover with a clean kitchen towel and rest 5 to 10 minutes. Serve from the pan with lemon wedges, scraping up the crispy bottom.

recipes.title: Irish Stew with Lamb and Potatoes
recipes.summary: A plain, pale Irish stew of lamb shoulder, onions, carrots and two kinds of potato simmered slowly until the floury ones melt into the broth. Simple, filling and better the next day.

ingredients.name: boneless lamb shoulder
ingredients.note: cut into 1½-inch chunks; or 3 lb bone-in lamb neck chops from a butcher or halal market, which is what most Irish cooks use

ingredients.name: russet potatoes
ingredients.note: peeled and cut into 1-inch chunks; these break down and thicken the stew

ingredients.name: yukon gold potatoes
ingredients.note: peeled and cut into large 2-inch chunks; these hold their shape

ingredients.name: carrots
ingredients.note: peeled and cut into thick 1½-inch pieces

ingredients.name: chicken stock
ingredients.note: low-sodium; or lamb stock, or plain water; check the label if you need it gluten-free

instructions: Trim off any big lumps of hard fat from the lamb, then season the chunks all over with the salt and pepper. Irish stew isn't browned; the meat goes straight into the pot, which keeps the broth clean and pale.

Put the lamb, onions and russet potatoes into a large Dutch oven or heavy pot. Tuck in the thyme and bay leaves and pour over the stock; it should just cover the meat, so top up with a little water if needed.

Bring slowly to a boil over medium heat, skimming off the grey foam that rises for the first few minutes. Turn the heat to low, cover and simmer very gently, with just a lazy bubble or two, for 1 hour.

Add the carrots and Yukon Gold potatoes, pushing them down into the liquid. Cover again and simmer for 45 minutes to 1 hour more, until the lamb is tender enough to break with a spoon, the large potatoes are cooked through and the russets have collapsed and thickened the broth.
Fish out the thyme stems and bay leaves. If the broth is still thin, crush a few pieces of potato against the side of the pot and stir them in. Taste and add more salt and pepper.

Stir in most of the parsley, ladle into wide bowls and scatter the rest on top. Serve with buttered soda bread or crusty bread if you like. It keeps 3 days in the fridge and tastes even better reheated.

recipes.title: Toad in the Hole with Onion Gravy
recipes.summary: Pork sausages baked in a tall, crisp Yorkshire pudding batter and served with a quick onion gravy. A cheap, cheerful midweek dinner ("tea" up North) that kids love.

ingredients.name: pork sausages
ingredients.note: fresh, thick and mild (about 1½ lb); British-style bangers from a British shop or butcher are best, or use plain fresh bratwurst rather than breakfast links or fennel-heavy Italian sausage

instructions: Heat the oven to 425°F. Whisk the flour and salt with the eggs to a smooth, thick paste, then gradually whisk in the milk until the batter is lump-free, about the thickness of heavy cream, with a few bubbles on top. Leave it to rest on the counter while the sausages cook.
Pour the oil into a 9x13-inch metal roasting pan (not glass, which can crack at this heat). Add the sausages, spaced apart, and roast for 12 to 15 minutes, turning once, until browned on two sides.
Working quickly, take the pan out, check the fat is smoking hot and spread the sausages out evenly. Give the batter a last whisk and pour it in around them; it should sizzle as it hits the pan.

Return to the oven straight away and bake for 25 to 30 minutes, until the batter has puffed high around the edges and is deep golden brown and crisp. Don't open the door for the first 20 minutes or it will sink.
While it bakes, melt the butter in a saucepan over medium-low heat and cook the onions with a pinch of salt, stirring now and then, for 15 to 20 minutes until soft and golden brown.

Stir the 2 tablespoons of flour into the onions and cook 1 minute, then gradually whisk in the stock and Worcestershire sauce. Simmer for 5 to 8 minutes, stirring, until glossy and thick enough to coat a spoon, then season with the pepper and more salt if needed.
Cut the toad in the hole into squares at the table and serve straight away with the onion gravy, mashed potatoes and peas or green beans.

recipes.title: Kedgeree (Smoked Haddock and Curried Rice)
recipes.summary: Buttery, gently spiced rice folded with flakes of smoked haddock, soft-boiled eggs, parsley and lemon. An Anglo-Indian breakfast that works just as well for supper; mild, not hot.

ingredients.name: smoked haddock
ingredients.note: undyed if you can find it; sold as finnan haddie at fish counters, British shops or online. Hot-smoked salmon or smoked trout also work: skip poaching, cook the rice in 2¼ cups water or light stock and flake the fish in at the end

ingredients.name: basmati rice
ingredients.note: rinsed until the water runs clear

ingredients.name: mild curry powder
ingredients.note: any mild supermarket curry powder; check the label if you need it gluten-free

ingredients.name: water
ingredients.note: for poaching the fish; you'll use it to cook the rice

ingredients.name: lemon
ingredients.note: half juiced, half cut into wedges

ingredients.name: salt
ingredients.note: only if needed; the fish is salty

instructions: Put the smoked haddock in a wide pan with the bay leaves and the 3 cups of water. Bring to a bare simmer and poach for 5 to 6 minutes, until the fish flakes easily. Lift it onto a plate and strain the poaching liquid into a measuring jug; you need 2¼ cups, so top up with water if short.
Meanwhile, bring a small pan of water to a boil, lower in the eggs and cook for 7 minutes for jammy yolks. Move them to a bowl of cold water.

Melt 2 tablespoons of the butter in a medium saucepan over medium heat and cook the onion for 5 minutes until soft and golden at the edges. Stir in the curry powder and turmeric for 30 seconds until fragrant, then add the rice and stir to coat every grain.

Pour in the 2¼ cups of poaching liquid, add the bay leaves back in, bring to a boil, then cover and cook on the lowest heat for 12 minutes. Take off the heat and leave covered for 5 minutes; the rice should be tender with all the liquid absorbed.
While the rice cooks, peel the eggs and cut them into quarters. Flake the haddock into large pieces, throwing away the skin and any bones.

Remove the bay leaves, fluff the rice with a fork and gently fold in the haddock, the remaining tablespoon of butter, the cream if using, the lemon juice and most of the parsley. Taste and add salt only if it needs it, plus the pepper.
Pile onto a warm platter, top with the eggs and the rest of the parsley and serve with lemon wedges.

recipes.title: Tex-Mex Cheese Enchiladas with Chili Gravy
recipes.summary: Corn tortillas softened in hot oil, rolled around cheddar and onion, smothered in a brick-red chili gravy and baked until bubbling, the plate every San Antonio cafe is built on. Mild; the heat is gentle and earthy.

ingredients.name: vegetable oil
ingredients.note: for the gravy; lard is traditional if you have it

ingredients.name: chili powder
ingredients.note: a Texas-style blend like Gebhardt if you can find it; any supermarket chili powder works

ingredients.name: mexican oregano
ingredients.note: sold in bags in the Hispanic spice aisle; or regular dried oregano

ingredients.name: chicken broth
ingredients.note: or beef broth; use vegetable broth to keep it vegetarian

ingredients.name: cheddar cheese
ingredients.note: shredded (1 lb); grate it from a block so it melts smoothly

instructions: Make the gravy: heat 1/4 cup oil in a medium saucepan over medium heat. Whisk in the flour and cook, whisking, until it smells toasty and turns light tan, 2 to 3 minutes.

Take the pan off the heat and whisk in the chili powder, cumin, garlic powder and oregano for 30 seconds so the spices bloom without scorching. Return to the heat and slowly whisk in the broth until smooth.

Simmer the gravy, whisking now and then, until it coats the back of a spoon like a thin pudding, 8 to 10 minutes. Season with salt. If it gets too thick, loosen with a splash of water. Heat the oven to 400°F.
Heat the 1/3 cup oil in a small skillet over medium heat. With tongs, dip each tortilla in the oil for 3 to 5 seconds per side, just until soft and pliable but not crisp, and drain on paper towels.

Spread about 1/2 cup gravy in a 9x13-inch baking dish. Lay a tortilla flat, fill it with about 1/4 cup cheese and a big pinch of onion, roll it up and set it seam side down in the dish. Repeat with the rest, packing them snugly.
Pour the remaining gravy over the enchiladas so every edge is covered, then scatter the last of the cheese and a little onion on top (save some raw onion for serving if you like).
Bake until the gravy bubbles at the edges and the cheese is melted, 12 to 15 minutes. Rest 5 minutes, then serve with rice, refried beans and pickled jalapeños.

recipes.title: Texas Chili con Carne (Bowl of Red)
recipes.summary: Cubed beef chuck simmered for hours in toasted ancho and guajillo chiles with cumin and garlic, and no beans, the way Texans make it. Medium heat from chiles de árbol; use one for a mild bowl.

ingredients.name: dried ancho chiles
ingredients.note: in the Hispanic aisle or produce section in bags; or 1/3 cup pure ancho chili powder

ingredients.name: dried guajillo chiles
ingredients.note: same aisle as the anchos; or use more anchos

ingredients.name: dried chiles de árbol
ingredients.note: the heat in the pot; use 1 for mild or 4 for hot; or 1/2 tsp cayenne

ingredients.name: beef broth
ingredients.note: check the label if you need it gluten-free

ingredients.name: ground cumin
ingredients.note: or 1 tbsp whole seeds, toasted and ground

ingredients.name: masa harina
ingredients.note: the corn flour for tortillas, in the Hispanic or baking aisle (Maseca); or a small handful of corn tortilla chips ground very fine

instructions: Pull the stems off the dried chiles and shake out most of the seeds. Toast them in a dry skillet over medium heat, pressing flat with a spatula, 20 to 30 seconds per side until fragrant and pliable; don't let them blacken or they turn bitter.
Put the chiles in a bowl, heat 2 cups of the broth until steaming and pour it over. Soak until soft, about 20 minutes, then blend the chiles and broth until completely smooth.

Meanwhile, pat the beef dry and toss with the salt. Heat the oil in a large Dutch oven over medium-high heat and brown the beef in 2 or 3 batches without crowding, 6 to 8 minutes per batch, until well browned on a couple of sides. Set each batch aside.
Lower the heat to medium, add the onion to the pot and cook, scraping up the browned bits, until soft, about 5 minutes. Stir in the garlic, cumin and oregano and cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Return the beef and its juices. Pour the chile purée through a mesh strainer into the pot, pressing on the solids, then add the tomato sauce and the remaining 2 cups broth. Bring to a boil.

Turn the heat to low, partly cover and simmer, stirring every 20 minutes or so, until a cube of beef breaks apart easily under a spoon, 2 1/2 to 3 hours. Add a splash of water if it gets thicker than a stew.
Whisk the masa harina with 1/4 cup water, stir it into the chili and simmer 10 minutes more until thick and glossy. Stir in the vinegar, taste and add salt.
Serve in bowls with warm corn tortillas or saltines (tortillas keep it gluten-free), chopped onion and shredded cheese on the side. It tastes even better the next day.

recipes.title: King Ranch Chicken Casserole
recipes.summary: Layers of corn tortillas, shredded chicken, peppers and diced tomatoes with green chiles in a creamy sauce, buried under cheddar and baked until bubbling. The potluck and funeral casserole of Texas; mild enough for kids.

ingredients.name: cooked chicken
ingredients.note: shredded; one supermarket rotisserie chicken is about right

ingredients.name: poblano pepper
ingredients.note: seeded and chopped; or a second green bell pepper

ingredients.name: diced tomatoes with green chiles
ingredients.note: 10-oz cans such as Ro-Tel, drained; pick the mild kind for kids; or a 14.5-oz can diced tomatoes plus a 4-oz can diced green chiles

ingredients.name: cheddar cheese
ingredients.note: shredded; half Monterey Jack is good too

instructions: Heat the oven to 350°F and butter a 9x13-inch baking dish.

Melt the butter in a large skillet or saucepan over medium heat. Add the onion, bell pepper and poblano and cook, stirring, until soft, 6 to 8 minutes. Stir in the garlic, cumin and chili powder and cook 1 minute.
Sprinkle in the flour and stir for 1 minute. Slowly whisk in the broth, then the milk, and simmer, stirring, until the sauce thickens enough to coat a spoon, 4 to 5 minutes.
Stir in the drained tomatoes with green chiles, the chicken and the salt. Taste; it should be well seasoned because the tortillas soak up salt.
Warm the tortillas in a dry skillet for about 20 seconds per side, or wrapped in a damp towel in the microwave for 45 seconds, so they hold together, then tear each into quarters.
Layer a third of the tortillas over the bottom of the dish, top with a third of the chicken mixture and a third of the cheese. Repeat twice, ending with cheese.

Cover with foil and bake 25 minutes, then uncover and bake until bubbling at the edges and golden on top, 15 to 20 minutes more. Let it rest 10 minutes so it slices cleanly, and top with green onions.

To make ahead, assemble, cover and refrigerate up to 1 day, adding 10 minutes to the covered baking time. It also freezes well, wrapped, for up to 3 months; thaw overnight in the fridge before baking.

recipes.title: Stovetop Chile con Queso
recipes.summary: Silky Tex-Mex cheese dip of deli white American and Monterey Jack with onion, jalapeño and tomato, ready in 20 minutes for game day. Mild to medium, depending on the jalapeño seeds.

ingredients.name: jalapeño
ingredients.note: seeded and minced for mild; keep the seeds or use 2 for more heat

ingredients.name: white american cheese
ingredients.note: ask for a thick slice at the deli counter and tear it up; it keeps the dip smooth

ingredients.name: salt
ingredients.note: to taste; the cheese is already salty

ingredients.name: corn tortilla chips
ingredients.note: for dipping; check the label if you need them gluten-free

instructions: Melt the butter in a medium saucepan over medium heat. Add the onion and jalapeño and cook until soft but not browned, about 4 minutes. Stir in the garlic and tomato and cook 1 minute more.

In a measuring cup, whisk the cornstarch into the evaporated milk until there are no lumps, then pour it into the pan. Heat, stirring, until it steams and thickens slightly, 2 to 3 minutes; don't let it boil hard.
Turn the heat to low and add the American cheese a handful at a time, stirring until each addition melts before adding more.
Stir in the Monterey Jack and cumin and keep stirring just until smooth and glossy, about 1 minute. Taste and add salt only if it needs it.

Pour into a warm bowl, top with cilantro and serve right away with tortilla chips. To keep it dippable at a party, hold it in a small slow cooker on warm, and stir in a splash of milk if it thickens. Reheat leftovers gently with a little milk.

recipes.title: Salat Katzutz (Israeli Chopped Salad)
recipes.summary: Cucumber, tomato and parsley cut into a tiny, even dice and dressed with lemon and olive oil. It sits on every Israeli table, from breakfast with eggs to a side for grilled meat.

ingredients.name: persian cucumbers
ingredients.note: or 1 English cucumber; leave the peel on

ingredients.name: red onion
ingredients.note: a small piece, very finely chopped; leave it out if your family doesn't like raw onion

ingredients.name: red bell pepper
ingredients.note: optional; some families always add it, some never do

ingredients.name: sumac
ingredients.note: tangy red spice; Middle Eastern grocers or the spice aisle; skip it or add a little extra lemon

instructions: Trim the ends of the cucumbers and cut them into 1/4-inch dice. Take your time: a fine, even dice is the whole point of this salad, and every piece should fit on a spoon with the others.
Core the tomatoes and cut them into the same small dice. Keep the seeds and juice; they become part of the dressing. Dice the bell pepper the same size if using.
Put the cucumbers, tomatoes, pepper, onion, parsley and mint in a bowl. You can cover and chill it like this for up to 3 hours.
Just before serving, add the lemon juice, olive oil, salt and pepper and toss well. Dressing it early draws water out of the vegetables and leaves them soggy.
Taste and adjust the salt and lemon; it should be bright and a little sharp. Sprinkle with sumac and serve right away, with pita to wipe up the juices.

recipes.title: Sabich Bowl with Roasted Eggplant, Egg and Tahini
recipes.summary: The Iraqi-Jewish Shabbat breakfast turned Tel Aviv street pita, served as a bowl: roasted eggplant, sliced eggs and potatoes over chopped salad with tahini and tangy amba.

ingredients.name: eggplants
ingredients.note: large globe eggplants, about 2 lb in all

ingredients.name: eggs
ingredients.note: if you made brown, slow-cooked haminados eggs for Shabbat, use those; that is the original Iraqi way

ingredients.name: tahini
ingredients.note: stir the jar well first; sold near the peanut butter or in the international aisle

ingredients.name: amba
ingredients.note: pickled mango sauce with fenugreek; Middle Eastern or kosher grocers, or online. Or thin mango chutney with lemon juice and a pinch each of turmeric and ground fenugreek

ingredients.name: dill pickles
ingredients.note: Israeli-style pickled cucumbers in brine (kosher aisle) or sour garlic dills, sliced

ingredients.name: pita bread
ingredients.note: to stuff or tear over the bowl

ingredients.name: schug
ingredients.note: Yemenite green chili-cilantro sauce, also spelled zhug or skhug; Middle Eastern grocers and some supermarket dip aisles. Adds real heat; or use any green hot sauce

instructions: Heat the oven to 450°F. Cut the eggplants into 1/2-inch rounds, brush both sides generously with the olive oil and sprinkle with 1 teaspoon of the salt. Spread on two parchment-lined sheet pans.
Roast for 25 to 30 minutes, flipping once halfway, until the slices are deep brown on both sides and completely soft and creamy inside. (Frying them in oil is the street-stall way, if you want to.)

Meanwhile, put the eggs and whole potatoes in a pot, cover with cold water and bring to a boil. Lift out the eggs after 10 minutes of boiling and drop them into cold water. Keep the potatoes going another 10 to 15 minutes until a knife slides in easily, then drain and cool slightly.

Make the tahini sauce: whisk the tahini, 2 tablespoons of the lemon juice, the garlic and 1/4 teaspoon salt. It will seize and thicken at first; keep whisking in cold water a little at a time until it is smooth, pale and pourable like heavy cream.
Toss the cucumbers, tomatoes and parsley with the remaining lemon juice and salt.
Peel and slice the eggs and the potatoes. Divide the chopped salad among four bowls and arrange the eggplant, egg and potato slices on top with the pickles.

Drizzle each bowl with plenty of tahini and a spoonful of amba, add schug if you like heat, and serve with warm pita. The eggplant, eggs and sauce keep 3 days in the fridge, so the bowls are easy to build for lunches.

recipes.title: Israeli Chicken Schnitzel with Sesame Crumbs
recipes.summary: Thin chicken breast cutlets in a crisp sesame-flecked crumb, pan-fried golden the way every Israeli mother makes them. Dairy-free, kid-approved, and great cold in a pita the next day.

ingredients.name: boneless skinless chicken breasts
ingredients.note: about 2 large; or use thin-sliced chicken cutlets and skip the pounding

ingredients.name: plain breadcrumbs
ingredients.note: fine dry breadcrumbs; panko works too for a crunchier coat

ingredients.name: vegetable oil
ingredients.note: for shallow pan-frying; enough for about 1/4 inch in a 12-inch skillet

instructions: Slice each chicken breast in half horizontally into two thin pieces. Lay them between sheets of plastic wrap and pound with a meat mallet or heavy pan to an even 1/4 inch. Season both sides with 1 teaspoon of the salt and the pepper.

Set up three shallow plates: the flour in the first; the eggs beaten with 2 tablespoons water, the garlic if using and the remaining 1/2 teaspoon salt in the second; the breadcrumbs mixed with the sesame seeds and paprika in the third.

Dredge each cutlet in flour and shake off the excess, dip it in egg and let the extra drip off, then press it into the crumbs on both sides so they stick. Lay the breaded cutlets on a tray. (You can freeze them raw at this point between sheets of parchment for up to 2 months and fry from frozen, adding 2 minutes.)

Heat the oil in a large heavy skillet over medium-high until a pinch of crumbs sizzles immediately, about 350°F. Fry 2 or 3 cutlets at a time without crowding, 2 to 3 minutes per side, gently swirling the pan now and then, until deep golden and crisp.

Check that the thickest piece reads 165°F, then move the schnitzels to a rack set over a sheet pan, or paper towels, and sprinkle with a pinch of salt while hot. Keep finished batches warm in a 200°F oven while you fry the rest, skimming out burnt crumbs between batches.
Serve hot with lemon wedges, mashed potatoes or ptitim and a chopped salad. Leftovers go cold into pita with hummus, salad and a little amba or ketchup.

recipes.title: Ptitim (Israeli Pearl Couscous) with Vegetables
recipes.summary: Toasted pearl couscous simmered with onion, carrot, zucchini and tomato paste until plump and tender. The one-pot weeknight side Israeli kids grow up on, ready in about 35 minutes.

ingredients.name: pearl couscous
ingredients.note: also sold as Israeli couscous, near the rice and pasta

ingredients.name: vegetable broth
ingredients.note: hot; many Israeli homes use pareve chicken-style soup powder in water, which is often vegan, so check the label

ingredients.name: salt
ingredients.note: less if your broth is salty

instructions: Heat the oil in a medium saucepan with a lid over medium heat. Add the onion and carrots and cook, stirring often, for 5 to 6 minutes until the onion is soft and turning golden at the edges.
Add the pearl couscous and stir for 2 to 3 minutes until many of the little balls are toasted light brown and smell nutty. This step keeps them separate and gives the dish its flavor.
Stir in the zucchini, garlic, tomato paste and paprika and cook 1 minute, until the paste coats everything and darkens slightly.

Pour in the hot broth, add the salt and pepper and bring to a boil. Cover, turn the heat to low and simmer for 10 to 12 minutes, until the liquid is absorbed and the couscous is tender with a slight chew. Scatter the peas on top for the last 3 minutes if using.
Take the pot off the heat and let it sit covered for 5 minutes, then fluff with a fork. If it looks dry, stir in a splash of hot water. Taste for salt, sprinkle with parsley and serve.

recipes.title: Pork Schnitzel Wiener Art
recipes.summary: Thin pork cutlets in a fine, puffy breadcrumb crust, shallow-fried in oil and butter until golden. The everyday Bavarian and Austrian version of Wiener Schnitzel, on the table in 30 minutes.

ingredients.name: boneless pork loin chops
ingredients.note: 4 thin chops, fat trimmed; or thin-sliced pork cutlets or chicken breast cutlets

ingredients.name: milk
ingredients.note: or heavy cream; makes the egg coat thinner

ingredients.name: plain dry breadcrumbs
ingredients.note: fine and unseasoned; or pulse panko in a blender until fine

ingredients.name: vegetable oil
ingredients.note: for shallow frying; or part lard, as many Austrian cooks use

ingredients.name: butter
ingredients.note: or clarified butter (ghee) in place of some of the oil

ingredients.name: lingonberry jam
ingredients.note: Austrian-style; find it at IKEA, European delis or the jam aisle; or whole-berry cranberry sauce

instructions: Put each chop between two sheets of plastic wrap and pound with a meat mallet or the bottom of a heavy pan until about 1/4 inch thick and evenly flat. Season both sides with the salt and pepper.
Set up three shallow plates: the flour; the eggs beaten with the milk and a pinch of salt until no streaks of white remain; and the breadcrumbs.

Dredge a cutlet in flour and shake off the extra, dip it in egg and let it drip, then lay it in the crumbs and turn it over. Don't press the crumbs on; a loose coat is what puffs up. Bread the cutlets just before frying so the crust stays dry.

Pour the oil into a 12-inch skillet (a good 3/16 inch deep) and add 1 tbsp of the butter. Heat over medium-high until a pinch of crumbs sizzles right away (about 340°F). The cutlets should float in the fat, not sit on the pan, so add a little more oil if your pan is wider.

Fry 2 cutlets at a time for 2 to 3 minutes per side, gently swirling the pan and spooning hot fat over the top so the crust lifts away from the meat in waves. They're done when deep golden on both sides and the pork reaches 145°F.
Drain on a rack or paper towels, add the rest of the butter to the pan and fry the second batch. Keep the first batch warm in a 200°F oven if you like.

Serve right away with lemon wedges to squeeze over, a spoon of lingonberry jam and parsley. In Vienna it comes with parsley potatoes or vinegar potato salad; in Swabia with Kartoffelsalat; a green salad works too.

recipes.title: Allgäuer Käsespätzle
recipes.summary: Homemade egg spätzle layered with melted Swiss cheese and Gruyère and topped with slow-fried golden onions. The cheesy Alpine dumpling dinner Bavarian and Swabian families make on cold nights.

ingredients.name: all-purpose flour
ingredients.note: about 13 oz; or 1 lb store-bought dried spätzle from the German import or pasta aisle, cooked by the package

ingredients.name: water
ingredients.note: plus 1 to 3 tbsp more if needed; some families use sparkling water or milk

ingredients.name: salt
ingredients.note: plus more for the cooking water

ingredients.name: swiss cheese
ingredients.note: Emmentaler if you can find it, coarsely grated; check for microbial rennet if you need it strictly vegetarian

ingredients.name: gruyere cheese
ingredients.note: coarsely grated; Allgäuer Bergkäse is the original, and a little Limburger adds the traditional funk

instructions: Whisk the flour, eggs, water, salt and nutmeg in a bowl, then beat hard with a wooden spoon for 3 to 5 minutes until the batter is smooth, stretchy and starts to bubble. It should be thick and drop slowly from the spoon in heavy blobs, not run; beat in more water a tablespoon at a time only if it's too stiff to press. Rest it 10 minutes.

Meanwhile, melt 3 tbsp of the butter in a large skillet over medium heat. Cook the onions with a pinch of salt, stirring now and then, for 20 to 25 minutes until deep golden brown and crisp at the edges. Lower the heat if they darken too fast.
Heat the oven to 200°F and put a buttered ovenproof dish in to warm. Bring a large pot of well-salted water to a gentle boil.

Press the batter into the water in batches with a spätzle maker, or push it through a colander with large holes using a spatula. The spätzle are done when they float, about 1 to 2 minutes; lift them out with a slotted spoon and shake off the water.

Layer the hot spätzle straight into the warm dish with handfuls of both cheeses and a grind of pepper after each batch, finishing with cheese. A spoonful of the cooking water over each layer keeps it creamy. Keep the dish in the oven between batches so the cheese melts into stretchy layers.

Dot with the last tbsp of butter, cover with a lid or foil and leave in the oven 5 to 10 minutes until the top cheese has melted. Pile the fried onions on top and scatter with chives. Serve hot with a green salad dressed with vinegar and oil.

recipes.title: Swabian Kartoffelsalat
recipes.summary: Southern German potato salad with no mayo: warm sliced waxy potatoes soaked in hot broth, vinegar, onion and mustard until silky. Make it ahead for schnitzel, sausages or a potluck.

ingredients.name: yukon gold potatoes
ingredients.note: or red potatoes; any waxy potato that holds its shape, similar size

ingredients.name: beef broth
ingredients.note: or vegetable broth to make it vegetarian; check the label if you need it gluten-free

ingredients.name: vegetable oil
ingredients.note: sunflower or canola; a neutral oil

ingredients.name: english cucumber
ingredients.note: very thinly sliced and salted, for the cucumber-potato version

instructions: Put the potatoes in their skins in a pot, cover with cold salted water and bring to a boil. Simmer 20 to 25 minutes until a knife slides in with only a little resistance at the center; don't let them go soft. Drain and let them steam a few minutes.
While the potatoes cook, bring the broth, diced onion, vinegar, mustard, sugar, salt and pepper to a boil in a small pot, then simmer 2 minutes so the onion softens.
Peel the potatoes while still hot (hold them with a fork or a kitchen towel) and slice them about 1/8 inch thick into a large bowl.
Pour the hot broth mixture over the warm slices and fold gently with a spatula. It will look too wet; that's right.
Cover and let stand at least 30 minutes, folding a couple of times, until the potatoes have drunk most of the liquid and the salad turns creamy and a little glossy.

Fold in the oil and chives (and the squeezed-dry cucumber, if using). Taste and add more salt, vinegar or a splash of warm broth if it seems dry. Serve lukewarm or at room temperature, not fridge-cold.

recipes.title: Bavarian Gulaschsuppe
recipes.summary: Beer-hall goulash soup: beef chuck simmered with a mountain of onions, sweet paprika, caraway and marjoram, with potatoes and red pepper. Rich and warming, not spicy unless you add hot paprika.

ingredients.name: sweet paprika
ingredients.note: Hungarian sweet paprika if you can, not smoked

ingredients.name: hot paprika
ingredients.note: for gentle heat; or a pinch of cayenne

ingredients.name: beef broth
ingredients.note: low-sodium; check the label if you need it gluten-free

instructions: Pat the beef dry and season with 1 tsp of the salt. Heat 2 tbsp of the oil in a large Dutch oven over medium-high heat and brown the beef in two batches, about 5 minutes per batch, until well browned on a couple of sides. Move to a bowl.
Lower the heat to medium, add the last tbsp of oil and the onions and cook, stirring and scraping up the browned bits, for 12 to 15 minutes until soft and golden.

Stir in the garlic and tomato paste and cook 2 minutes until the paste darkens. Take the pot off the heat, stir in both paprikas, the caraway and marjoram (paprika burns and turns bitter over high heat), then splash in the vinegar.
Return the beef and its juices, add the broth and bay leaves and bring to a boil. Cover, lower the heat and simmer gently for 1 hour 15 minutes, stirring now and then.
Add the potatoes and bell pepper and simmer uncovered 25 to 30 minutes until the beef is fork-tender and some of the potato breaks down to thicken the soup.

Fish out the bay leaves, season with the remaining salt, the pepper and the lemon zest if using. Serve in deep bowls with crusty rolls or rye bread. It's even better the next day and freezes for up to 3 months.

recipes.title: Phyllo Apfelstrudel
recipes.summary: Viennese apple strudel made the weeknight way with store-bought phyllo: tart cinnamon apples, raisins and buttery toasted breadcrumbs rolled in crackly layers. Lovely warm with vanilla sauce or whipped cream.

ingredients.name: phyllo dough
ingredients.note: sheets (about 9 by 14 inches), thawed overnight in the fridge; in the freezer aisle

ingredients.name: tart apples
ingredients.note: about 5, such as Granny Smith, or half Honeycrisp; peeled, cored and thinly sliced

ingredients.name: raisins
ingredients.note: soaked 15 minutes in warm water or rum, then drained

ingredients.name: butter
ingredients.note: unsalted; 2 tbsp for the crumbs and 8 tbsp melted for brushing

instructions: Heat the oven to 375°F and line a large rimmed baking sheet with parchment. Melt 2 tbsp of the butter in a skillet over medium heat and toast the breadcrumbs, stirring, for 3 to 4 minutes until golden and nutty-smelling. Let cool. Melt the remaining 8 tbsp butter.
Toss the apples with the lemon juice, sugar, cinnamon, drained raisins and walnuts if using. Make this just before rolling so the apples don't release too much juice.

Lay a clean kitchen towel on the counter. Keeping the rest of the phyllo covered with a damp towel, lay one sheet on the towel with a long side facing you and brush it lightly with melted butter. Stack 5 more sheets on top, brushing each one.

Sprinkle half the toasted crumbs over the bottom two-thirds of the stack, leaving a 1-inch border at the sides. Spoon half the apples (leave the juice in the bowl) in a log along the long edge nearest you. Don't overfill: the phyllo needs to wrap all the way around once with some overlap.

Fold the side edges in over the filling, then lift the towel to roll the strudel away from you into a snug log. Roll it seam side down onto the baking sheet. Repeat with the remaining phyllo, crumbs and apples for a second strudel.

Brush both strudels all over with the rest of the butter and cut 3 or 4 small slits in the tops. Bake 35 to 40 minutes until deep golden and crisp and the apples are tender when you poke a knife through a slit.
Cool at least 15 minutes, dust thickly with powdered sugar and slice with a serrated knife. Serve warm with vanilla sauce, whipped cream or vanilla ice cream.

recipes.title: Argentine Baked Beef Empanadas
recipes.summary: Baked half-moon pastries stuffed with a juicy filling of beef, slow-cooked onion, paprika, cumin, green onion and chopped egg. Freeze well and feed a crowd; only a whisper of heat.

ingredients.name: ground beef
ingredients.note: 85% lean, or finely dice 1.5 lb chuck by hand for the knife-cut style

ingredients.name: green onions
ingredients.note: white and green parts separated, thinly sliced

ingredients.name: vegetable oil
ingredients.note: or beef fat or lard, as many abuelas use

ingredients.name: crushed red pepper
ingredients.note: ají molido; leave out for kids

ingredients.name: raisins
ingredients.note: a family-by-family argument; in Córdoba most families add them and sprinkle a little sugar on top before baking. Skip if you're not sure

ingredients.name: empanada discs
ingredients.note: for baking (para horno), about 5 in across; Goya or La Salteña in the freezer aisle at Latin grocers and many supermarkets; thaw in the fridge. Or use 3 refrigerated pie crusts cut into 5-in rounds

instructions: Heat the oil in a large skillet over medium-low heat. Add the onions, bell pepper, green onion whites and 1 tsp salt and cook slowly, stirring now and then, for 15 to 20 minutes until very soft and sweet but not browned.

Turn the heat to medium-high, add the beef and break it up with a spoon. Cook just until it loses its pink color, 5 to 6 minutes; don't let it brown and dry out. Stir in the paprika, cumin, crushed red pepper, oregano, black pepper and remaining 1 tsp salt and cook 1 minute more.

Take the pan off the heat, stir in the green onion tops and taste: it should be well seasoned, a little saltier than you'd eat it alone. Spread the filling on a sheet pan and refrigerate until completely cold, at least 1 hour or overnight, so the fat sets and the empanadas stay juicy.
Heat the oven to 400°F and line 2 sheet pans with parchment. Stir the chopped egg (and olives and raisins, if using) into the cold filling.

Put a heaping 2 tablespoons of filling in the center of a disc, wet the edge with a fingertip of water, fold it into a half-moon and press out the air. Seal with the repulgue (fold and pinch the edge over itself all the way around) or crimp with a fork. Don't overfill or they'll burst.
Set the empanadas on the pans, brush with beaten egg and bake 18 to 22 minutes, swapping the pans halfway, until deep golden on top and lightly browned underneath.
Rest 5 minutes before eating; the inside is very hot and juicy. To freeze, freeze unbaked empanadas on a tray, bag them, and bake from frozen for 25 to 30 minutes.

recipes.title: Milanesa a la Napolitana
recipes.summary: Thin breaded beef cutlets fried until crisp, then topped with tomato sauce, ham and melted mozzarella under the broiler. The Buenos Aires bodegón classic, usually served with fries.

ingredients.name: beef top round
ingredients.note: sliced into 4 thin cutlets (milanesa cut); ask the butcher, or use top round steak. For suprema a la napolitana, use 2 large chicken breasts split in half

ingredients.name: plain breadcrumbs
ingredients.note: fine and unseasoned (pan rallado), not panko

ingredients.name: vegetable oil
ingredients.note: for shallow frying, about 1/8 inch deep in a 10-inch skillet; top up between cutlets as needed

instructions: Put each cutlet between sheets of plastic wrap and pound it to an even 1/4 inch. Beat the eggs in a shallow dish with the garlic, parsley, 1 tsp salt and the pepper, add the cutlets, turn to coat and let them sit 15 minutes (or up to overnight in the fridge).
Meanwhile, simmer the crushed tomatoes with the olive oil, 1 tsp oregano and remaining 1/2 tsp salt in a small saucepan for 10 minutes until thick enough to hold its shape on a spoon.

Spread the breadcrumbs on a plate. Lift each cutlet from the egg, press it firmly into the crumbs on both sides, dip it back in the egg and press into the crumbs again; the double coat is what makes it crisp. Set on a rack.
Heat the broiler with a rack about 6 inches from the heat. Heat the vegetable oil in a 10-inch skillet over medium-high until a pinch of crumbs sizzles right away, about 350°F.
Fry the milanesas one at a time, 2 to 3 minutes per side, until deep golden and crisp. Drain on paper towels and sprinkle with a little salt.
Move the milanesas to a sheet pan. Spread each with 2 or 3 tablespoons of sauce, lay a slice of ham on top, then cover with mozzarella and sprinkle with the remaining oregano.
Broil 2 to 4 minutes until the cheese is melted and spotted brown. Serve right away with French fries or mashed potatoes and lemon wedges.

recipes.title: Locro Criollo
recipes.summary: A thick, slow-simmered stew of white hominy, white beans, squash, pork, beef and chorizo, eaten on May 25 and July 9. Mild itself; spoon on the red paprika-onion oil for gentle heat.

ingredients.name: dried white hominy
ingredients.note: maíz blanco pisado or mote pelado; find it at Latin grocers or online. Or use three 29-oz cans, drained, and add them with the squash

ingredients.name: dried great northern beans
ingredients.note: or two 15-oz cans, drained, added with the squash

ingredients.name: bacon
ingredients.note: thick-cut, diced; stands in for panceta

ingredients.name: spanish chorizo
ingredients.note: cured, sliced; or fresh Argentine-style chorizo, browned and sliced

ingredients.name: green onions
ingredients.note: thinly sliced, for the red oil

ingredients.name: crushed red pepper
ingredients.note: for the red oil; use less for milder

instructions: The night before, put the hominy and beans in a large bowl, cover with plenty of cold water and soak overnight. Drain.

In a large heavy pot (at least 8 quarts) over medium heat, cook the bacon until the fat runs, 5 minutes. Add the pork and beef and cook, stirring, until no longer pink, about 8 minutes. Add the onions and cook 5 minutes until soft, then stir in 1 tbsp paprika and the cumin.

Add the drained hominy and beans and about 12 cups of water, enough to cover by 2 inches. Bring to a boil, skim off any foam, then lower to a gentle simmer, partly covered, for 2 hours, stirring the bottom every 15 minutes so it doesn't stick.

Add the squash, chorizo and salt with 2 more cups of water if it looks dry. Simmer another 1 to 1 1/2 hours, stirring often, until the hominy is tender and burst, the squash has collapsed into the broth and the stew is thick enough for a spoon to stand up in it.

For the red oil (quiquirimichi), warm the vegetable oil in a small pan over low heat, add the green onions and cook 2 minutes until soft. Off the heat, stir in the remaining 2 tbsp paprika and the crushed red pepper; don't let the paprika burn or it turns bitter.

Taste the locro for salt and serve in deep bowls with a spoonful of red oil on top. It thickens as it sits; thin with a little water when reheating. It's better the next day and freezes well for 3 months.

recipes.title: Grilled Provoleta
recipes.summary: A thick round of provolone seared on the grill or in a cast-iron skillet until crusty outside and molten inside, dusted with oregano and chili flakes. The classic opener at an asado.

ingredients.name: provolone
ingredients.note: one round slab about 3/4 to 1 inch thick, cut from a whole provolone at the deli counter; aged (piccante) holds its shape best

instructions: Chill the cheese in the freezer for 15 to 20 minutes so it gets very firm; this keeps it from melting into a puddle before it crusts. Rub off the wax rind if it has one.
Heat a grill to medium-high with a small cast-iron skillet or provoletera on the grate, or heat a cast-iron skillet on the stove over medium-high heat, for 5 minutes until very hot.

Sprinkle the top of the cheese with half the oregano and crushed red pepper. Put it in the dry pan seasoned side down and sprinkle the rest on top. Don't touch it for 3 to 4 minutes, until the bottom has a dark golden crust and releases from the pan.
Slide a thin metal spatula under it and flip it quickly. Cook 2 to 3 minutes more until the second side is crusty and the center is soft and bulging when pressed.
Drizzle with olive oil and serve straight from the pan with crusty bread and chimichurri if you like. Eat it right away, before it firms up.

recipes.title: Alfajores de Maicena
recipes.summary: Tender, crumbly cornstarch cookies sandwiched with dulce de leche and rolled in coconut. The alfajor every Argentine grandmother makes for merienda; they keep for days.

ingredients.name: brandy
ingredients.note: or cognac; many families add it, but leave it out for a kids' batch

ingredients.name: dulce de leche
ingredients.note: thick (repostero) style from Latin grocers, or Nestlé La Lechera dulce de leche in the baking aisle

ingredients.name: shredded coconut
ingredients.note: unsweetened, finely shredded (desiccated) is what Argentines use; sweetened works too

instructions: Whisk the cornstarch, flour, baking powder and baking soda in a bowl. In a large bowl, beat the butter and sugar with a mixer until pale and creamy, 2 to 3 minutes, then beat in the yolks one at a time, followed by the vanilla, lemon zest and brandy, if using.
Add the dry ingredients and mix on low, then finish with your hands just until it comes together into a soft, smooth dough; don't overwork it. Flatten into a disc, wrap and refrigerate 30 minutes.

Heat the oven to 350°F and line 2 sheet pans with parchment. On a lightly floured surface, roll the dough 1/4 inch thick and cut 2-inch rounds, rerolling the scraps once. Space them 1 inch apart on the pans.

Bake one pan at a time for 8 to 10 minutes, until set and dry on top but still pale; the bottoms should be barely golden. They'll feel soft but firm up as they cool. Cool on the pan 5 minutes, then on a rack until completely cool; handle gently, they're fragile.
Spread about 2 teaspoons of dulce de leche on the flat side of half the cookies and top with the rest, pressing gently so the filling reaches the edges.
Roll the edges in coconut so it sticks to the dulce de leche. Let them sit for a few hours (or overnight) so the cookies soften into the filling. Keep in an airtight container for up to 5 days.

recipes.title: Doro Wot
recipes.summary: Ethiopia's holiday stew of chicken and whole eggs in a deep berbere and onion sauce, shortened to about 2 1/2 hours. Hot with 1/4 cup market berbere; for medium use 2 tbsp berbere plus 2 tbsp paprika.

ingredients.name: chicken legs
ingredients.note: bone-in drumsticks and thighs, skin removed

ingredients.name: niter kibbeh
ingredients.note: Ethiopian spiced clarified butter, sold in jars at Ethiopian markets and online. Quick version: melt 10 tbsp unsalted butter with 1 tbsp chopped onion, 1 crushed garlic clove, 1 tsp grated ginger, 1/2 tsp each fenugreek seeds and cumin seeds, 1/4 tsp turmeric and 2 crushed cardamom pods; keep it on the lowest heat 20 minutes until the solids turn golden, then strain (makes about 1/2 cup). Ghee with a pinch of cardamom works in a pinch

ingredients.name: berbere
ingredients.note: Ethiopian chili spice blend; sold at Ethiopian and East African markets, spice shops, many Whole Foods and online. Brands vary a lot in heat (market blends are often hotter than supermarket jars), so taste a pinch first. For medium heat use 2 tbsp berbere plus 2 tbsp sweet paprika, which keeps the deep red color. Quick stand-in (medium, milder than most market berbere): 3 tbsp sweet paprika, 2 tsp cayenne, 1 tsp each ground ginger, coriander and fenugreek, 1/2 tsp black pepper and 1/4 tsp each cardamom, cinnamon, cloves and allspice (makes about 1/3 cup); add more cayenne for true heat

ingredients.name: ground cardamom
ingredients.note: or korerima (Ethiopian cardamom) from an Ethiopian market

ingredients.name: injera
ingredients.note: sourdough teff flatbread from Ethiopian markets and some international aisles; it freezes well. 100% teff injera is gluten-free, but many US loaves blend in wheat or barley, so check the label

ingredients.name: cottage cheese
