ingredients.note: drained in a fine sieve; the closest US stand-in for ayib, the fresh cheese served alongside to cool the heat (farmer's cheese also works)

instructions: Cut a few shallow slashes in each chicken piece. Soak the chicken for 10 minutes in a bowl of cold water with the lemon juice and 1 tsp of the salt, then drain and rinse. Meanwhile hard-boil the eggs for 10 minutes, cool them in cold water and peel.

Pulse the onions in a food processor until very finely minced but not puréed. Cook them in a large Dutch oven over medium heat with no fat, stirring often, until their liquid has cooked off and they have shrunk by about half and turned soft and light brown, 30 to 40 minutes. If they catch, lower the heat and add a splash of water, not oil.

Stir in 1/4 cup of the niter kibbeh and cook 5 minutes. Add the berbere and the tomato paste, if using, and cook over medium-low for 10 to 15 minutes, stirring often and adding 2 to 3 tbsp water whenever it starts to stick, until you have a dark brick-red paste with butter pooling at the edges.

Stir in the garlic and ginger for 2 minutes. Add the chicken and turn it to coat, then add 1 1/2 cups water and the remaining 1 tsp salt. Bring to a simmer, cover and cook on low for 35 to 40 minutes, turning the pieces now and then, until the chicken is tender and reads 175°F at the bone.

Score the peeled eggs lightly all over with a knife so the sauce can soak in. Nestle them into the pot with the rest of the niter kibbeh and the cardamom and simmer uncovered for 10 minutes, until the sauce coats a spoon like thick gravy. Loosen with a little of the remaining water if it gets too tight.

Taste for salt. Serve each person a piece of chicken and an egg with plenty of sauce, on injera or with rice, with the cheese on the side. It tastes even better the next day and keeps 4 days in the fridge.

recipes.title: Gomen (Ethiopian Collard Greens)
recipes.summary: Collard greens braised slowly with onion, garlic and ginger until silky, finished with strips of green chile. A fasting-day staple that goes with every wot; mild, with a little fresh heat.

ingredients.name: vegetable oil
ingredients.note: on non-fasting days some cooks swap in a spoonful of niter kibbeh (then it is no longer vegan)

ingredients.name: jalapeno
ingredients.note: seeded and cut into thin strips; use 1 Anaheim chile for milder

instructions: Wash the collards well in a sink of cold water. Strip the leaves off the stems, stack and roll them, slice into thin ribbons, then cut across into small pieces.
Heat the oil in a large pot over medium heat. Cook the onion, stirring, until soft and golden, 6 to 8 minutes. Add the garlic and ginger and cook 1 minute until fragrant.

Add the collards a few handfuls at a time, stirring until each batch wilts. Add the salt and 1 cup water, cover and simmer over medium-low for 25 to 30 minutes, stirring now and then, until the greens are tender and dark olive green. Add a splash of water if the pot goes dry.
Uncover, add the jalapeno strips and cook 5 minutes more, until most of the liquid has cooked off and the greens look glossy.
Taste for salt and add lemon juice if you like. Serve warm or at room temperature beside a wot or misir on injera or rice. It keeps 4 days in the fridge.

recipes.title: Shiro Wot
recipes.summary: A smooth, savory stew of spiced ground chickpeas simmered with onion, garlic and tomato, ready in half an hour. The everyday Ethiopian supper; medium heat, depending on your shiro blend.

ingredients.name: vegetable oil
ingredients.note: on non-fasting days, some cooks replace 2 tbsp with niter kibbeh (then it is no longer vegan)

ingredients.name: tomato
ingredients.note: medium, finely chopped, or 1 tbsp tomato paste

ingredients.name: shiro powder
ingredients.note: roasted ground chickpeas and spices, sold at Ethiopian markets and online. Stand-in: toast 1 cup chickpea flour in a dry skillet, stirring, until it smells nutty, 3 to 4 minutes, then mix in 2 tsp berbere and 1/2 tsp each garlic powder and ground ginger. Check the label if you need it gluten-free

ingredients.name: salt
ingredients.note: many shiro blends are already salted, so taste first

ingredients.name: berbere
ingredients.note: for more heat; Ethiopian chili spice blend from Ethiopian markets, spice shops or online

ingredients.name: jalapeno
ingredients.note: slit lengthwise, to lay on top

ingredients.name: injera
ingredients.note: sourdough teff flatbread from Ethiopian markets and some international aisles; it freezes well. 100% teff injera is gluten-free, but many US loaves blend in wheat or barley, so check the label

instructions: Put the onion in a medium saucepan over medium heat with no oil and cook, stirring, until soft and just starting to stick, about 5 minutes. Add the oil and cook 3 minutes more, until the onion is golden at the edges.
Add the garlic, tomato and berbere, if using, and cook 4 to 5 minutes, until the tomato collapses into a jammy sauce.
Pour in 3 cups of the water and bring to a simmer. Whisking constantly, sprinkle in the shiro powder a couple of spoonfuls at a time so no lumps form.

Turn the heat to low and partly cover, as it splutters. Simmer 10 to 15 minutes, whisking often and adding the remaining water a splash at a time, until the shiro is smooth and glossy, pours like thick gravy, has lost its raw bean taste and has little beads of oil on the surface.
Taste for salt and lay the jalapeno on top. Serve hot with injera, crusty bread or rice. Shiro thickens as it cools, so loosen leftovers with hot water.

recipes.title: Tikil Gomen
recipes.summary: Cabbage, potatoes and carrots cooked down with turmeric, garlic and ginger until soft and sweet. A gentle, golden vegetable stew that kids like; no heat unless you add chile.

ingredients.name: carrots
ingredients.note: peeled and cut into thick coins

ingredients.name: green cabbage
ingredients.note: small (about 2 lb), cored and cut into 1-inch pieces

ingredients.name: injera
ingredients.note: sourdough teff flatbread from Ethiopian markets and some international aisles; it freezes well. 100% teff injera is gluten-free, but many US loaves blend in wheat or barley, so check the label

instructions: Heat the oil in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium heat. Cook the onion, stirring, until soft and golden, 6 to 8 minutes.
Stir in the garlic, ginger and turmeric and cook 1 minute, until fragrant and the oil turns bright yellow.
Add the carrots, potatoes and salt and stir to coat them in the turmeric oil. Cook 5 minutes, stirring now and then.

Pile in the cabbage and add 1/2 cup water. Cover and cook over medium-low for 20 to 25 minutes, stirring every 5 minutes or so, until the potatoes are tender when pierced with a knife and the cabbage is soft and sweet. Add a splash of water if it starts to stick.
Uncover, add the jalapeno strips if using and cook 3 to 5 minutes to cook off most of the liquid. Taste for salt.
Serve warm with injera or rice, as a main with salad or alongside doro wot or misir wot. It keeps 4 days in the fridge.

recipes.title: Siga Tibs
recipes.summary: Cubes of beef seared hot and tossed with onion, rosemary, jalapeno, tomato and a spoonful of niter kibbeh: the sizzling pan Ethiopians order to share, done in under 30 minutes. Medium heat; seed the chiles for mild.

ingredients.name: beef sirloin
ingredients.note: or ribeye, trimmed and cut into 3/4-inch cubes

ingredients.name: niter kibbeh
ingredients.note: Ethiopian spiced clarified butter from Ethiopian markets or online; or ghee or butter with a pinch of ground cardamom

ingredients.name: berbere
ingredients.note: for a red, awaze-style tibs; Ethiopian chili spice blend from Ethiopian markets, spice shops or online

ingredients.name: injera
ingredients.note: sourdough teff flatbread from Ethiopian markets and some international aisles; it freezes well. 100% teff injera is gluten-free, but many US loaves blend in wheat or barley, so check the label

instructions: Pat the beef dry with paper towels and toss it with the salt and pepper.

Heat the oil in your largest skillet, cast iron if you have it, over high heat until it shimmers. Add the beef in a single layer, in two batches if it won't fit, and leave it 2 minutes to brown. Stir and cook 1 to 2 minutes more, until browned outside but still pink in the middle, then move it to a plate.
Turn the heat to medium-high, add the onion to the same pan and cook 3 minutes, until the edges char and soften a little. Add the garlic and rosemary and stir for 30 seconds.

Return the beef and its juices to the pan with the niter kibbeh, jalapeno, tomato and berbere, if using. Toss for 2 to 3 minutes, until the butter sizzles, the chiles are bright and just soft, and the beef is done how you like it; many Ethiopian families like it cooked through.
Serve straight from the pan while it's sizzling, with injera or rice and gomen or a simple tomato salad.

recipes.title: Nasi Goreng Jawa (Javanese Fried Rice with Chicken)
recipes.summary: Day-old jasmine rice fried with a shallot, garlic and chili paste, chicken and sweet soy, topped with a crisp-edged fried egg. Medium heat; halve the sambal for kids.

ingredients.name: cooked jasmine rice
ingredients.note: cold, ideally a day old; break up the clumps with your hands

ingredients.name: shallots
ingredients.note: peeled and roughly chopped; or 1/2 small red onion

ingredients.name: sambal oelek
ingredients.note: chili paste (Huy Fong is in most supermarkets' Asian aisle); or pound 2 fresh red Fresno chilies with a pinch of salt; sriracha works but is sweeter and garlicky

ingredients.name: shrimp paste
ingredients.note: terasi or belacan, from Asian grocers; gives the savory depth of street-cart nasi goreng; skip it if you can't find it

ingredients.name: kecap manis
ingredients.note: Indonesian sweet soy sauce (ABC or Bango), in Asian grocers and many supermarkets' international aisle; or simmer equal parts soy sauce and dark brown sugar for 2 minutes until syrupy

ingredients.name: fried shallots
ingredients.note: bawang goreng, sold in tubs at Asian grocers

instructions: Pound or blitz the shallots, garlic, sambal oelek and shrimp paste (if using) to a coarse paste in a mortar or mini chopper. Stir the kecap manis and soy sauce together in a small bowl, and crumble the rice so no clumps are left.

Heat 1 tbsp of the oil in a wok or large nonstick skillet over medium-high heat. Fry the eggs, two at a time, for 2 to 3 minutes, until the whites are set with lacy brown edges and the yolks are still runny. Set them aside.
Add the remaining 3 tbsp oil and the paste and fry over medium heat, stirring, for 2 to 3 minutes, until it darkens a shade and smells sweet rather than raw.
Turn the heat to high, add the chicken and salt, and stir-fry for 4 to 5 minutes, until the chicken is no longer pink and is starting to brown.
Add the rice and toss, pressing it against the pan, for 3 to 4 minutes, until it's hot through, the grains are separate and a few have caught and crisped.

Pour the kecap mixture around the edge of the pan, add the white pepper and toss for 1 to 2 minutes, until every grain is evenly glossy brown. Taste and add salt or a little more kecap manis, then stir in the green onions.
Pile the rice on plates, top each with a fried egg and serve with cucumber and tomato on the side, and fried shallots and shrimp crackers if you have them.

recipes.title: Beef Rendang
recipes.summary: Beef chuck simmered for about three hours in coconut milk and a chili, galangal and lemongrass paste until the sauce cooks down to a dark, clinging coat. Medium-hot; even better the next day.

ingredients.name: beef chuck
ingredients.note: cut into 2-inch chunks; chuck stays juicy through the long cook

ingredients.name: dried red chilies
ingredients.note: such as chiles de árbol or Asian dried chilies, stemmed and soaked in hot water for 15 minutes; or 1/4 cup sambal oelek; shake out the seeds of half for milder

ingredients.name: shallots
ingredients.note: peeled (about 1 1/2 cups sliced); or 1 large red onion

ingredients.name: galangal
ingredients.note: fresh or frozen, from Asian grocers, sliced; or 1 tbsp jarred galangal paste; or 2 more inches of ginger plus a squeeze of lime

ingredients.name: lemongrass
ingredients.note: bottom 6 inches, tough outer layers removed; or 2 tbsp lemongrass paste from the produce section (plus the zest of 1/2 lime)

ingredients.name: makrut lime leaves
ingredients.note: also sold as kaffir lime leaves, fresh or frozen at Asian grocers; or 3 wide strips of lime zest

ingredients.name: unsweetened shredded coconut
ingredients.note: desiccated or finely shredded, from the baking or natural-foods aisle; toasted and pounded into kerisik, the Malaysian way of thickening and darkening the sauce (many Padang kitchens skip it and simply cook the coconut milk down longer)

ingredients.name: tamarind paste
ingredients.note: seedless concentrate from Asian or Latin grocers; or 1 tbsp lime juice

instructions: Drain the chilies. Slice 1 stalk of lemongrass and bruise the other 2 with the back of a knife. Blend the chilies, shallots, garlic, ginger, galangal, turmeric and sliced lemongrass with 1/4 cup of the water until smooth.

Toast the coconut in a dry skillet over medium-low heat, stirring constantly, for 5 to 7 minutes, until evenly deep golden brown. Pound it in a mortar or grind it in a spice grinder until it turns into a dark, oily, clumpy paste. This is kerisik; set it aside.

Heat the oil in a heavy Dutch oven over medium heat. Add the paste, cinnamon, star anise, bruised lemongrass and lime leaves (tear them first) and fry, stirring often, for 8 to 10 minutes, until the paste darkens, thickens and the oil starts to separate.

Add the beef and stir for 2 minutes to coat. Add the coconut milk, the remaining 3/4 cup water, tamarind, palm sugar and salt and bring to a boil. Lower the heat and simmer uncovered, stirring and scraping the bottom every 15 minutes.
After about 2 hours, the beef should be nearly tender and the sauce reduced to a thick gravy (at this stage it's called kalio, and some families stop here). Stir in the kerisik.

Keep cooking for another 45 to 75 minutes, now stirring every 5 minutes as it thickens and lowering the heat if it catches, until the sauce has cooked down to a dark brown paste that clings to the beef, oil pools around the edges and the beef is fork-tender.

Taste for salt and sugar and fish out the cinnamon, star anise and lemongrass. Rest for 15 minutes, or cool and refrigerate overnight for deeper flavor, and serve with rice. It keeps 4 days in the fridge and 3 months frozen.

recipes.title: Gado-Gado (Vegetable Salad with Peanut Sauce)
recipes.summary: Jakarta-style salad of blanched vegetables, potatoes, fried tofu and tempeh and boiled eggs under a thick homemade peanut sauce. Mild; add more sambal to taste.

ingredients.name: extra-firm tofu
ingredients.note: one block, pressed dry and cut into 1-inch cubes

ingredients.name: tempeh
ingredients.note: one block, sliced 1/4 inch thick; in the refrigerated tofu section

ingredients.name: roasted peanuts
ingredients.note: unsalted; or 2/3 cup natural creamy peanut butter

ingredients.name: sambal oelek
ingredients.note: chili paste (Huy Fong is in most supermarkets' Asian aisle); or pound 2 fresh red Fresno chilies with a pinch of salt; sriracha works but is sweeter and garlicky; check the label and avoid sambal terasi or 'sambal belacan', which contain shrimp paste

ingredients.name: kecap manis
ingredients.note: Indonesian sweet soy sauce (ABC or Bango), in Asian grocers and many supermarkets' international aisle; or simmer equal parts soy sauce and dark brown sugar for 2 minutes until syrupy

ingredients.name: tamarind paste
ingredients.note: seedless concentrate from Asian or Latin grocers; or 1 more tbsp lime juice

ingredients.name: fried shallots
ingredients.note: bawang goreng, sold in tubs at Asian grocers

instructions: Put the potatoes in a pot of cold salted water, bring to a boil and cook for 15 to 18 minutes, until a knife slides in. Lower the eggs in for the last 9 minutes. Lift both out, cool the eggs in cold water, then peel and quarter them.

In the same boiling water, blanch the green beans for 3 minutes, the cabbage for 1 to 2 minutes and the bean sprouts for 20 seconds, scooping each out into a colander once it's bright and just tender-crisp.

Pat the tofu and tempeh dry. Heat the oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat and fry the tofu, turning, for 8 to 10 minutes, until golden and crisp on several sides. Fry the tempeh for 2 to 3 minutes per side, until golden brown. Drain both on paper towels and sprinkle with 1/2 tsp salt.

For the sauce, pulse the peanuts in a food processor to fine, sandy crumbs (stop before it turns to butter). Add the garlic, sambal oelek, kecap manis, tamarind, brown sugar, the remaining salt and half the lime juice, then blend in the hot water.

Pour the sauce into a small saucepan and simmer over low heat, stirring, for 2 to 3 minutes, until glossy and thick enough to coat a spoon. Loosen with a splash of water if needed and taste: it should be nutty, sweet, a little sour and salty, so adjust with lime juice, kecap manis or salt.
Arrange the potatoes, vegetables, cucumber, tofu, tempeh and eggs on a platter. Spoon the warm sauce over just before eating, scatter with fried shallots and toss it all together at the table.

recipes.title: Mee Goreng Mamak (Malaysian Fried Noodles with Shrimp)
recipes.summary: Malaysian mamak-stall noodles: fresh yellow noodles wok-fried with shrimp, tofu, potato and egg in a sweet, tangy chili-tomato sauce, finished with lime. Medium-hot.

ingredients.name: fresh yellow noodles
ingredients.note: Hokkien or Malaysian yellow noodles from the refrigerator case at Asian grocers; or fresh lo mein noodles; or 12 oz dried spaghetti cooked just short of al dente

ingredients.name: firm tofu
ingredients.note: half a block, cubed and patted dry; or a handful of fried tofu puffs

ingredients.name: yukon gold potato
ingredients.note: boiled until tender, peeled and cut into chunks; leftover is perfect, or prick it and microwave for 4 to 5 minutes until a knife slides in

ingredients.name: choy sum
ingredients.note: cut into 2-inch pieces; or baby bok choy

ingredients.name: sambal oelek
ingredients.note: chili paste (Huy Fong is in most supermarkets' Asian aisle); or pound 2 fresh red Fresno chilies with a pinch of salt; sriracha works but is sweeter and garlicky; use 1 tbsp for medium-mild

ingredients.name: kecap manis
ingredients.note: Indonesian sweet soy sauce (ABC or Bango), in Asian grocers and many supermarkets' international aisle; or simmer equal parts soy sauce and dark brown sugar for 2 minutes until syrupy

ingredients.name: limes
ingredients.note: cut into wedges; or calamansi if you find them

instructions: If the noodles are stiff from the fridge, rinse them briefly in hot water and drain well. Stir the sambal oelek, ketchup, kecap manis, soy sauce and oyster sauce (if using) with 2 tbsp water.

Heat 1 tbsp of the oil in a wok or 12-inch skillet over high heat. Fry the tofu for about 4 minutes, until golden on a few sides, then push it aside, add the shrimp and cook about 1 minute per side, until just pink. Take both out.

Add the remaining 2 tbsp oil, the shallots and garlic and stir for 30 seconds, until fragrant but not brown. Add the tomato and potato and stir-fry for 1 minute, breaking the potato up a little so it thickens the sauce.
Add the noodles and sauce and toss for 2 to 3 minutes, until the noodles have soaked up the sauce and a few strands are charring.
Push the noodles to one side, crack the eggs into the space and scramble until just set, then toss them through the noodles.

Return the shrimp and tofu, add the choy sum and bean sprouts and toss for 1 to 2 minutes, until the greens wilt but the sprouts are still crunchy. Taste and add more kecap manis for sweetness or sambal for heat.
Serve right away with lime wedges to squeeze over.

recipes.title: Ayam Kecap (Sweet Soy Braised Chicken)
recipes.summary: Chicken browned, then braised in kecap manis with shallots, garlic, candlenuts and ginger until glossy and sticky. Sweet, savory and mild, the one kids ask for; add whole chilies for heat.

ingredients.name: candlenuts
ingredients.note: kemiri, from Indonesian or Southeast Asian grocers; or 4 raw macadamia nuts or 5 raw cashews

ingredients.name: kecap manis
ingredients.note: Indonesian sweet soy sauce (ABC or Bango), in Asian grocers and many supermarkets' international aisle; or simmer equal parts soy sauce and dark brown sugar for 2 minutes until syrupy

ingredients.name: nutmeg
ingredients.note: ground; a pinch, as my mother does

ingredients.name: thai chilies
ingredients.note: bird's eye chilies, left whole and pricked, for heat

ingredients.name: fried shallots
ingredients.note: bawang goreng, sold in tubs at Asian grocers

instructions: Rub the chicken with the lime juice and salt and leave it for 15 minutes. Meanwhile, blend the shallots, garlic, candlenuts and ginger with 2 tbsp of the water to a fairly smooth paste.

Pat the chicken dry. Heat the oil in a large, deep skillet or braiser over medium-high heat and brown the chicken skin side down for 6 to 8 minutes, until deep golden, then flip for 2 minutes and take it out. Pour off all but about 2 tbsp of the fat.
Fry the paste over medium heat, stirring, for 4 to 5 minutes, until it's lightly golden, starting to stick and no longer smells of raw shallot.

Add the kecap manis, soy sauce, white pepper and nutmeg (if using) and stir for 30 seconds, just until it bubbles; it burns fast. Add the rest of the water and the chilies (if using) and return the chicken, skin side up.

Cover and simmer gently for 20 minutes. Uncover, add the tomato and simmer 10 to 15 minutes more, spooning the sauce over the chicken, until the sauce has reduced to a glossy, syrupy glaze and the chicken reads 175°F near the bone.
Scatter in the green onions for the last 2 minutes. Serve with rice, topped with fried shallots if you like. It's even better reheated the next day.

recipes.title: Gyeran-bap (Korean Soy-Butter Egg Rice)
recipes.summary: Hot rice topped with a runny fried egg, butter, soy sauce, sesame oil and crumbled roasted seaweed, mixed together in the bowl. Ten minutes and kids ask for it by name.

ingredients.name: cooked short-grain rice
ingredients.note: leftover is fine; calrose or any sticky white rice

ingredients.name: soy sauce
ingredients.note: Korean ganjang if you have it; any regular soy sauce works

ingredients.name: roasted seaweed snacks
ingredients.note: small gim or nori snack pack, in the Asian aisle; or half a sheet of nori

ingredients.name: kimchi
ingredients.note: on the side for the grown-ups; most kimchi has fish sauce or salted shrimp, so pick a vegan one for vegetarians

instructions: Reheat the rice until it is steaming hot all the way through. In the microwave, cover it with a damp paper towel and heat 1 to 2 minutes. Divide it between two bowls.
Heat the oil in a nonstick skillet over medium heat. Crack in the eggs and fry 2 to 3 minutes, until the whites are set and the edges are lacy and crisp but the yolks are still runny.
Drop 1 teaspoon of butter onto each bowl of hot rice so it starts to melt, then slide an egg on top.
Drizzle each bowl with 1 teaspoon soy sauce and 1/2 teaspoon sesame oil. Crumble the seaweed over with your fingers and scatter on the green onion and sesame seeds.
Break the yolk and stir everything together right in the bowl until the rice is glossy and evenly seasoned. Taste and add a few more drops of soy sauce if needed. Serve with kimchi on the side.

recipes.title: Chilaquiles Verdes con Huevo
recipes.summary: Corn tortilla chips simmered for a minute in tangy tomatillo salsa, then topped with fried eggs, crema, queso fresco and onion. Mild to medium heat, depending on your salsa.

ingredients.name: salsa verde
ingredients.note: one 16-oz jar such as Herdez; or blend 1 lb boiled tomatillos with 1 serrano, 1 garlic clove, 1/4 onion and a handful of cilantro

ingredients.name: water
ingredients.note: or chicken broth if you don't need it vegetarian

ingredients.name: corn tortilla chips
ingredients.note: the thick, sturdy kind; or cut 12 day-old corn tortillas into sixths and fry them in oil until crisp

ingredients.name: crema mexicana
ingredients.note: dairy case or Latin aisle; or sour cream thinned with a splash of milk

instructions: Pour the salsa verde and water into a 12-inch skillet and bring to a lively simmer over medium heat, 3 to 4 minutes. Taste and add salt if it needs it; jarred salsas vary.
While the salsa heats, warm the oil in a second skillet over medium heat and fry the eggs 2 to 3 minutes, until the whites are set and the yolks are as runny as your family likes.
Have the plates and toppings ready before the chips go in, because chilaquiles wait for no one.

Add the chips to the bubbling salsa and fold gently with a spatula for 1 to 2 minutes, until every chip is coated and the edges have softened but the centers still have some bite. Simmer a minute longer if your house likes them soft.
Divide among plates right away. Drizzle with crema, scatter queso fresco, onion and cilantro over, and top each plate with a fried egg. Serve with avocado and refried beans on the side.

recipes.title: Kanda Poha (Onion and Peanut Flattened Rice)
recipes.summary: Maharashtra's everyday breakfast: rinsed flattened rice tossed with mustard seeds, curry leaves, onion, peanuts and turmeric, finished with lemon. Light heat from one green chile.

ingredients.name: thick poha
ingredients.note: flattened rice labeled thick or medium, at Indian grocers or online; thin poha turns to mush

ingredients.name: raw peanuts
ingredients.note: skin-on or skinned; or roasted unsalted peanuts added at the end

ingredients.name: black mustard seeds
ingredients.note: Indian grocers; or yellow mustard seeds

ingredients.name: asafoetida
ingredients.note: hing, at Indian grocers; most brands are cut with wheat flour, so use one labeled gluten-free to keep it gluten-free

ingredients.name: curry leaves
ingredients.note: fresh, at Indian grocers; leave out if you can't find them

ingredients.name: serrano chile
ingredients.note: slit lengthwise; seed it or leave it out for kids

ingredients.name: grated coconut
ingredients.note: fresh or frozen, at Indian grocers

instructions: Put the poha in a colander and rinse under cold running water for 15 to 20 seconds, tossing with your fingers, just until every flake is wet. Drain well, sprinkle with the salt and sugar, toss gently and leave 5 minutes. A flake should squash easily between your fingers but the poha should still look like separate flakes.
Heat the oil in a wide skillet or kadai over medium heat. Fry the peanuts, stirring, 2 to 3 minutes until they smell toasty and the skins darken. Lift them out with a slotted spoon.
Add the mustard seeds to the same oil. When they start to pop, add the cumin seeds, asafoetida, curry leaves and chile and stir for 20 to 30 seconds.
Add the onion and cook 3 to 4 minutes, stirring, until soft and translucent but not browned. Stir in the turmeric for a few seconds.
Tip in the poha and peanuts and fold gently with a flat spatula until the poha is evenly yellow. Don't stir hard or it breaks up.
Turn the heat to low, cover and let it steam 2 minutes, until hot through and fluffy.
Turn off the heat, squeeze over the lemon juice and fold in the cilantro. Serve topped with coconut and sev, with lemon wedges and hot chai.

recipes.title: Tamagoyaki (Sweet Rolled Japanese Omelette)
recipes.summary: Layers of lightly sweet, soy-seasoned egg rolled up in the pan and sliced into neat pieces. Great warm at breakfast and keeps two days for lunch boxes.

ingredients.name: sugar
ingredients.note: use 2 tsp for a less sweet omelette

ingredients.name: mirin
ingredients.note: Asian aisle; or another 1/2 tsp sugar

ingredients.name: water
ingredients.note: or cooled dashi for a savory dashimaki style; regular dashi is made with fish, so use kombu dashi to keep it vegetarian

instructions: Crack the eggs into a bowl and beat with chopsticks, cutting through the whites with side-to-side strokes rather than whisking air in. Add the sugar, soy sauce, mirin, water and salt and stir until the sugar dissolves. Pour through a strainer for a smoother omelette if you like.
Heat a rectangular tamagoyaki pan or an 8-inch nonstick skillet over medium heat. Fold a paper towel, dip it in the oil and wipe the pan. A drop of egg should sizzle gently, not spit.

Pour in about a quarter of the egg and tilt to cover the pan. Pop any big bubbles. When the bottom is set but the top is still a little wet, after 30 to 60 seconds, roll the egg from the far side toward you in 3 or 4 folds with chopsticks or a thin spatula.

Push the roll back to the far side. Wipe the empty part of the pan with the oiled towel, pour in another quarter of the egg and lift the roll so egg runs underneath it. When it is nearly set, roll toward you again, wrapping the new layer around the first.
Repeat with the rest of the egg in two more layers. If the egg browns before it sets, turn the heat down; sugar browns fast, and a light golden color is fine.
Tip the roll onto a bamboo mat, plastic wrap or a clean towel, wrap it snugly and press into a neat rectangle. Rest 3 to 5 minutes so it sets.
Slice into 8 pieces and serve warm with rice and miso soup, or cool completely, cover and refrigerate up to 2 days for bento.

recipes.title: Longsilog (Sweet Longganisa, Garlic Rice and Egg)
recipes.summary: Homemade skinless sweet pork longganisa with garlic fried rice and a fried egg, the Filipino silog breakfast. Roll a batch of longganisa on Sunday and freeze it for school mornings.

ingredients.name: ground pork
ingredients.note: 80/20, not lean, or the sausages dry out

ingredients.name: brown sugar
ingredients.note: packed; sweet longganisa should taste clearly sweet

ingredients.name: garlic
ingredients.note: minced; 5 for the longganisa and 8 for the rice

ingredients.name: cane vinegar
ingredients.note: Filipino Datu Puti or Silver Swan in the Asian aisle; or white vinegar

ingredients.name: salt
ingredients.note: 1 tsp for the longganisa, 1/2 tsp for the rice

ingredients.name: cooked white rice
ingredients.note: day-old and cold, so it fries without clumping; jasmine is typical

ingredients.name: spiced vinegar
ingredients.note: sukang maanghang for dipping; or cane vinegar with a little garlic and black pepper

instructions: Put the pork, brown sugar, 5 cloves of the garlic, soy sauce, vinegar, paprika, pepper and 1 teaspoon salt in a bowl. Mix with your hands for about 1 minute, until sticky and evenly blended. If you have time, cover and refrigerate a few hours or overnight so the flavor deepens.

Divide the mixture into 12 pieces and shape each into a 3-inch log. Roll each tightly in a square of wax paper or plastic wrap and twist the ends. To freeze, lay them on a tray until hard, then bag them for up to 3 months.

Unwrap the longganisa into a nonstick skillet, add 1/3 cup water, cover and simmer over medium heat for 5 minutes (8 to 10 minutes from frozen). Uncover, let the water cook off, then fry in the rendered fat with 1 teaspoon oil, turning often, 5 to 7 minutes until sticky, caramelized and 160°F inside. Turn the heat down if the sugar starts to blacken.

Meanwhile, break up the cold rice with damp hands. In a wok or large skillet, heat 2 tablespoons oil over medium-low and cook the remaining 8 cloves of garlic, stirring, 2 to 3 minutes until light golden. Spoon out half the garlic to sprinkle on top.
Turn the heat to high, add the rice and 1/2 teaspoon salt and toss 4 to 5 minutes, until steaming hot with a few toasty grains.
In another skillet, fry the eggs in the remaining oil over medium heat until the edges are crisp and the yolks still runny, 2 to 3 minutes.
Plate a mound of garlic rice topped with the reserved garlic, 3 longganisa and an egg, with sliced tomato and a small dish of spiced vinegar for dipping.

recipes.title: Xôi Xéo (Turmeric Sticky Rice with Mung Bean and Fried Shallots)
recipes.summary: Hanoi's street breakfast: golden steamed sticky rice with thin shavings of mung bean paste, crisp fried shallots and shallot oil. Soak the night before; it reheats well all week.

ingredients.name: glutinous rice
ingredients.note: labeled sweet rice or glutinous rice, at Asian grocers; regular rice won't stick

ingredients.name: turmeric
ingredients.note: ground; or 1 tbsp grated fresh turmeric

ingredients.name: split mung beans
ingredients.note: peeled yellow ones, at Asian grocers or sold as moong dal at Indian grocers

instructions: The night before, rinse the rice in several changes of water until it runs nearly clear. Cover with 2 inches of water, stir in the turmeric and soak 6 to 8 hours. Rinse the mung beans and soak them in a separate bowl of water for at least 2 hours or overnight.

In the morning, drain the rice well and toss it with 1/2 teaspoon salt. Line a steamer basket with damp cheesecloth or perforated parchment, spread the rice in an even layer and poke a few holes in it with a chopstick.

Steam, covered, over boiling water for 25 to 30 minutes. Halfway through, toss the rice and sprinkle it with 2 tablespoons water. It is done when the grains are shiny, chewy and translucent with no hard white center.

Meanwhile, drain the mung beans, cover with water by 1/2 inch, add 1/2 teaspoon salt and simmer 15 to 20 minutes until completely soft and the water is gone. Mash to a smooth, thick paste while hot (or pulse in a food processor), then squeeze it into a tight ball.

Put the shallots and oil in a small saucepan, set over medium heat and cook, stirring often, 8 to 10 minutes until evenly golden. Scoop them onto a paper towel right away, since they keep darkening off the heat, and sprinkle with the last 1/4 teaspoon salt. Save the oil.
Toss the hot rice with 2 tablespoons of the shallot oil. Scoop portions into bowls, then hold the mung bean ball over each one and shave thin slices over the rice with a sharp knife.

Drizzle with a little more shallot oil and pile on the fried shallots. In Hanoi meat-eaters often add pork floss on top. Refrigerate leftover rice and mung bean up to 3 days; reheat the rice covered in the microwave with a splash of water.

recipes.title: Arepas de Queso (Colombian Cheese Arepas)
recipes.summary: Griddled corn cakes made from precooked cornmeal with melty cheese worked into the dough, crisp outside and soft inside. Cook a double batch and freeze them for school mornings.

ingredients.name: precooked white cornmeal
ingredients.note: masarepa such as P.A.N. or Goya, in the Latin aisle; masa harina and regular cornmeal won't work

ingredients.name: shredded mozzarella
ingredients.note: or queso blanco or quesito colombiano from a Latin grocer

instructions: Stir the warm water, salt and melted butter together in a large bowl. Pour in the cornmeal gradually, mixing with your hand to break up lumps, until it comes together. Let it rest 5 minutes to hydrate.
Knead in the cheese. The dough should be soft and smooth, like play dough; if it cracks when you press it, work in more warm water a tablespoon at a time.
Divide into 8 balls. Pat each between your palms into a disk about 3 1/2 inches across and 1/2 inch thick, and smooth any cracked edges with a wet finger.

Heat a cast-iron skillet or griddle over medium-low and wipe it with the oil. Cook the arepas in batches, 6 to 8 minutes per side, until golden with darker spots, and they sound hollow when tapped. Too-high heat burns the outside before the middle cooks.
Serve hot with a pat of butter and a pinch of salt, alongside eggs or hot chocolate.

To freeze, cool the cooked arepas, stack them with parchment between and bag for up to 2 months. Reheat from frozen in a 400°F toaster oven for 10 to 12 minutes, or in a covered skillet over medium-low.

recipes.title: Pannukakku (Finnish Oven Pancake)
recipes.summary: A thin, custardy pancake baked in one pan and cut into squares with strawberry jam and cream. Finns eat it after Thursday pea soup; it makes an easy weekend brunch too.

ingredients.name: strawberry jam
ingredients.note: the Finnish classic; or raspberry, blueberry or lingonberry jam

instructions: Heat the oven to 425°F. Whisk the eggs, sugar and salt in a large bowl, then whisk in the flour and about 1 cup of the milk to a smooth paste. Whisk in the rest of the milk and the cardamom. The batter will be very thin; if you have time, let it rest 20 to 30 minutes.
Put the butter in a 9-by-13-inch metal pan and set it in the oven for 3 to 4 minutes, until melted and sizzling. Don't let it brown too far.
Take the pan out, tilt it so the butter coats the bottom and sides, and pour in the batter. Some butter will pool on top; that's how the edges crisp.
Bake 25 to 30 minutes, until puffed, golden-brown around the edges and set in the center. A knife pushed into the middle should come out without liquid egg.
It will sink as it cools; that's normal. Let it settle 5 minutes, cut into squares and serve warm with strawberry jam and whipped cream.

recipes.title: Syrniki / Syrnyky (Farmer's Cheese Pancakes)
recipes.summary: Thick little pancakes made mostly of farmer's cheese, golden outside and tender like cheesecake inside, eaten with sour cream and jam in Ukraine (where they're syrnyky) and Russia. They freeze well.

ingredients.name: farmer's cheese
ingredients.note: tvorog, such as Friendship or Lifeway, in the dairy aisle or at Eastern European delis; or ricotta drained overnight, plus a little more flour

ingredients.name: all-purpose flour
ingredients.note: about 1/3 cup in the dough and the rest for coating

ingredients.name: vegetable oil
ingredients.note: sunflower oil is traditional; or half oil, half butter

instructions: Mash the farmer's cheese in a bowl with a fork until it is fine and crumbly with no big lumps. For extra-smooth syrniki, push it through a sieve.

Mix in the egg, sugar, salt and vanilla, then about 1/3 cup flour and the raisins. The dough should be soft and slightly sticky but hold its shape. If it is very wet, add flour a tablespoon at a time; too much makes them dry and tough.

Put the remaining flour on a plate. Scoop 2 heaped tablespoons of dough, roll into a ball in the flour, then flatten into a 3/4-inch-thick patty and straighten the sides with a knife. You should get about 12.

Heat the oil in a large skillet over medium-low. Fry the syrniki 3 to 4 minutes per side, until deep golden and they feel springy when pressed. If they brown faster than that, lower the heat so the middle warms through.
Drain briefly on a paper towel and serve warm with sour cream and jam.
To freeze, set the shaped, floured syrniki on a floured tray until firm, then bag for up to 2 months. Fry from frozen over low heat, covered for the first side, 5 to 6 minutes per side.

recipes.title: Mangú con Cebollitas (Dominican Mashed Plantains)
recipes.summary: Boiled green plantains mashed smooth with butter and cold water, topped with vinegary sautéed red onions. Add fried salami, cheese and eggs for los tres golpes.

ingredients.name: green plantains
ingredients.note: fully green and firm; Latin grocers and most supermarkets

ingredients.name: dominican salami
ingredients.note: sliced 1/4 inch thick; Induveca or Campesino brand at Latin grocers, or any firm cooking salami

ingredients.name: queso de freír
ingredients.note: frying cheese, sliced 1/2 inch thick; Latin grocers, or halloumi

instructions: Cut the ends off the plantains, slit the skin lengthwise along the ridges and pry it off with your thumb. Cut the plantains into 2-inch chunks.
Put them in a pot, cover with water by an inch, add 2 teaspoons salt and boil 15 to 20 minutes, until a fork slides in with no resistance.

While they cook, warm the olive oil in a skillet over medium heat and cook the onion 3 to 4 minutes, until just softened but still pink. Add the vinegar and a pinch of salt, simmer 1 minute and set aside.

For los tres golpes, while the plantains finish boiling, fry the salami and cheese slices in a dry or lightly oiled skillet over medium heat for 2 to 3 minutes per side until browned, then fry the eggs in the same pan. Keep everything warm on a plate.

Drain the plantains and mash them right away, while very hot, with the butter, the remaining 1/2 teaspoon salt and 1/2 cup of the cold water. Keep adding cold water a splash at a time and mashing until smooth and creamy, like loose mashed potatoes. Mangú stiffens as it cools, so don't wait.
Spoon the mangú onto plates, top with the onions and their vinegar, and serve with the salami, cheese and eggs.

recipes.title: Kiribath with Lunu Miris (Sri Lankan Coconut Milk Rice)
recipes.summary: Rice cooked soft in coconut milk, set into squares and served with lunu miris, a pounded onion and chili sambol. The rice is mild; the sambol is very hot, so kids can have theirs with banana.

ingredients.name: short-grain white rice
ingredients.note: Sri Lankan white raw rice from South Asian grocers, or sushi rice

ingredients.name: salt
ingredients.note: 1 1/2 tsp for the rice, 1/2 tsp for the sambol

ingredients.name: red chili flakes
ingredients.note: Sri Lankan chili flakes from South Asian grocers are hottest; use 2 tsp for less heat

ingredients.name: maldive fish flakes
ingredients.note: dried tuna flakes from South Asian grocers; leave out for vegetarians

ingredients.name: banana
ingredients.note: and a little brown sugar or jaggery, for kids

instructions: Rinse the rice until the water runs clear. Put it in a heavy pot with the water, bring to a boil, then cover and cook on low for 15 minutes, until the water is absorbed and the rice is very soft. Slightly overcooked is right here.
Stir in the coconut milk and 1 1/2 teaspoons salt. Cook uncovered over low heat, stirring often, 8 to 10 minutes until the rice is thick, creamy and pulls away from the sides of the pot in one mass.
Spread it on a lightly oiled plate or an 8-inch square dish about 1 inch thick. Smooth the top with a piece of banana leaf, an oiled spatula or the back of a spoon dipped in water.
Let it cool 10 minutes, then cut into diamonds with an oiled knife.

For the lunu miris, pound the onion, chili flakes, Maldive fish and 1/2 teaspoon salt in a mortar to a rough, juicy paste, or pulse in a mini chopper. Stir in the lime juice and taste: it should be hot, salty and sour.
Serve the warm kiribath with a small spoonful of lunu miris on each piece, or with banana and a sprinkle of jaggery for kids.
Kiribath keeps covered at room temperature for a few hours or in the fridge for 2 days. It firms up cold; sprinkle with water and microwave until soft and warm.

recipes.title: Khagina (Pakistani Masala Scrambled Eggs)
recipes.summary: Soft scrambled eggs cooked into a quick masala of onion, tomato, green chile and cumin, scooped up with paratha or toast. Medium heat; on the table in under 20 minutes.

ingredients.name: vegetable oil
ingredients.note: or ghee, which won't be dairy-free

ingredients.name: serrano chiles
ingredients.note: finely chopped; or Indian green chilies

ingredients.name: red chili powder
ingredients.note: South Asian grocers; or 1/4 tsp cayenne plus 1/4 tsp paprika

ingredients.name: paratha
ingredients.note: frozen ones from South Asian grocers, cooked; or toast. Both have wheat, so serve with rice or corn tortillas for gluten-free

instructions: Heat the oil in a nonstick skillet over medium heat. Add the cumin seeds and let them sizzle for 20 seconds until fragrant.
Add the onion and cook, stirring, about 4 minutes until soft and just golden at the edges.
Add the tomato, chiles, turmeric, chili powder and salt. Cook 2 to 3 minutes, mashing the tomato with the spoon, until it collapses into a thick masala and the oil shines at the edges.

Beat the eggs well. Lower the heat to medium-low, pour them in and leave for 20 seconds, then stir in slow, wide folds for 2 to 3 minutes until the eggs form soft curds that are just set but still glossy. Take the pan off the heat while they look slightly wet; they finish cooking on the plate.
Scatter with cilantro and serve hot with paratha or toast and a cup of chai.

recipes.title: Slow Cooker Dal Makhani
recipes.summary: Punjabi black lentils and kidney beans cooked all day until creamy, then finished with a buttery cumin-onion tadka and a little cream. Mild, rich and freezes beautifully.

ingredients.name: whole black urad dal
ingredients.note: also sold as sabut urad or whole black gram at Indian grocers or online; not the split white kind. Soak 8 hours or overnight

ingredients.name: canned kidney beans
ingredients.note: 1 can, drained and rinsed; canned is safer than dried here because a slow cooker on LOW doesn't get hot enough to make dried kidney beans safe

ingredients.name: tomato sauce
ingredients.note: 1 can plain tomato sauce, or 1 1/2 cups passata; not pasta sauce. Goes in at the end: acid keeps the dal from softening

ingredients.name: kashmiri chili powder
ingredients.note: mild and bright red, at Indian grocers; or 1 tsp paprika plus a pinch of cayenne

ingredients.name: kasuri methi
ingredients.note: dried fenugreek leaves, at Indian grocers; leave out if you can't find it

instructions: The night before, rinse the urad dal in a few changes of water and soak it in a big bowl with plenty of water to cover by 3 inches. Forgot? Cover it with boiling water in the morning and let it sit for 1 hour.

In the morning, drain the dal and put it in the slow cooker with the kidney beans, water, 2 tbsp of the butter and the salt. Stir. It will look very watery; the dal soaks up most of it. Keep the tomato out for now: acid stops whole urad from turning soft and creamy.

Cover and cook on LOW for 9 to 10 hours or HIGH for 6 to 7 hours, until the dal is completely soft and a grain crushes to paste between your fingers. Older dal can take an hour longer. In an Instant Pot, use Slow Cook on More with the lid vented and allow the LOW timing, since it runs cooler than most slow cookers.
Mash the dal against the side of the pot with a potato masher or the back of a ladle for a minute so some of the lentils break and the pot turns creamy. Turn the cooker to HIGH.

For the masala, melt the remaining 2 tbsp butter in a skillet over medium heat. Add the cumin seeds and let them sizzle for 20 seconds, then add the onion and cook, stirring, for 7 to 8 minutes until golden at the edges. Stir in the ginger and garlic for 1 minute, then the chili powder for 15 seconds.

Pour in the tomato sauce and cook, stirring often, for 8 to 10 minutes until it thickens, darkens and the butter starts to separate at the edges. Stir in the garam masala and scrape it all into the dal.

Stir in the cream and crumble in the kasuri methi between your palms. Cook uncovered on HIGH for 30 minutes, stirring once or twice, so the masala melts into the dal. If it's thinner than a thick soup, give it another 15 minutes; if it's too thick, loosen it with a splash of hot water. Taste for salt.
Serve with rice, naan or roti, a swirl of cream and cilantro. It thickens in the fridge, so add water when you reheat. Freeze in portions for up to 3 months.

recipes.title: Slow Cooker Gigantes Plaki (Greek Baked Giant Beans)
recipes.summary: Big creamy white beans slow-cooked with olive oil and vegetables all day, then baked in tomato, oregano and dill until the top blisters. A cheap, hearty vegan main.

ingredients.name: dried gigantes beans
ingredients.note: sold as gigantes or elephant beans at Greek and Mediterranean grocers or online; large dried lima beans (butter beans) are the easy swap. Soak overnight

ingredients.name: extra virgin olive oil
ingredients.note: Greek cooks don't skimp, it makes the sauce

ingredients.name: water
ingredients.note: about enough to just cover the beans

instructions: The night before, soak the beans in a large bowl with water to cover by 4 inches; they more than double.

In the morning, drain the beans, put them in a pot with fresh water to cover and boil hard for 10 minutes, then drain. Don't skip this: a slow cooker doesn't get hot enough on its own to break down the natural lectins in big dried beans.

Put the beans in the slow cooker with the onion, carrot, celery, garlic, bay leaves, water and 1 tsp salt. The water should only just cover the beans. Leave the tomatoes and oil out for now: acid keeps beans from softening, and the oil would only be drained away.

Cover and cook on LOW for 7 to 8 hours or HIGH for about 4 hours, until the beans are creamy all the way through. Taste three or four to be sure; one firm bean means another 30 minutes, and old beans can take an hour or two longer.

Heat the oven to 425°F. Scoop out and save 1 cup of the cooking liquid, then drain the rest and discard the bay leaves. Stir the crushed tomatoes, tomato paste, sugar, oregano, olive oil, most of the parsley and dill, the pepper and the remaining 1/2 tsp salt into the beans and vegetables with 1/2 cup of the saved liquid.

Spread in a 9x13-inch baking dish and bake for 25 to 30 minutes, until the sauce is bubbling and thick and the beans on top are blistered and browned at the edges. Add a splash more liquid if it looks dry before then.
No time for the oven? Stir the sauce into the slow cooker instead and cook uncovered on HIGH for 45 to 60 minutes until thick.
Rest 10 minutes and top with the rest of the herbs. Serve warm or at room temperature with crusty bread, olives and a block of feta if you're not keeping it vegan. Freezes well for 3 months.

recipes.title: Slow Cooker Hong Shao Rou (Red-Braised Pork Belly)
recipes.summary: Shanghai-style pork belly glazed in caramelized sugar, soy and Shaoxing wine, then braised until it wobbles and reduced to a sticky, glossy sauce. Rich, sweet-savory and mild.

ingredients.name: pork belly
ingredients.note: skin-on if you can find it, cut into 1 1/2-inch cubes; Asian grocers sell it in slabs

ingredients.name: rock sugar
ingredients.note: crushed, from Asian grocers; or 3 tbsp granulated sugar

ingredients.name: shaoxing wine
ingredients.note: Chinese cooking wine in the Asian aisle; or dry sherry

ingredients.name: dark soy sauce
ingredients.note: for color, in the Asian aisle (Lee Kum Kee, Pearl River Bridge); or 1 more tbsp soy sauce plus 1 tsp molasses

ingredients.name: green onions
ingredients.note: whites cut into 2-inch lengths for the pot, greens sliced to serve

ingredients.name: cinnamon stick
ingredients.note: small, or a piece of cassia bark

ingredients.name: eggs
ingredients.note: hard-boiled and peeled, to braise in the sauce

instructions: Put the pork in a pot, cover with cold water and bring to a boil. Boil 3 minutes, until gray scum rises, then drain, rinse and pat dry. This keeps the sauce clean and glossy instead of murky.
Wipe out the pot, add the oil and fry the pork over medium heat for 5 to 6 minutes, turning, until the edges are golden and some fat has run out. Pour off all but about 1 tbsp of fat.

Add the rock sugar and stir for 2 to 3 minutes as it melts and turns amber, coating every piece (stand back; it spits). In a rush you can skip the caramel and add the sugar straight to the slow cooker, but the pork will be paler and less deep.

Pour in the Shaoxing wine, let it bubble for 30 seconds and scrape everything into the slow cooker. Add both soy sauces, the ginger, green onion whites, star anise, cinnamon, chilies if using, and the hot water. The liquid only comes about a third of the way up; the pork gives off plenty more.

Cover and cook on LOW for 6 to 7 hours or HIGH for 3 1/2 to 4 hours, until a chopstick slides through the skin and lean layers with no push. Tuck the eggs into the sauce for the last hour if you like.

Lift the pork (and eggs) into a bowl with a slotted spoon. Pour the liquid into a skillet or wok, spoon off most of the fat, and boil over high heat for 5 to 8 minutes until syrupy and it coats a spoon with big glossy bubbles. Taste and add a splash of soy if needed.
Return the pork to the sauce and toss to glaze. Serve over steamed rice with bok choy and the green onion tops. It keeps 4 days and reheats well, but the texture of the fat suffers in the freezer.

recipes.title: Slow Cooker Beef Nihari
recipes.summary: Pakistani beef shank slow-cooked in a spiced gravy until it falls off the bone, finished silky with toasted flour and piled with fried onion and ginger. Medium-hot.

ingredients.name: beef shank
ingredients.note: bone-in cross-cut slices; or 2 1/2 lb boneless chuck in large chunks

ingredients.name: vegetable oil
ingredients.note: many families use ghee, which makes it no longer dairy-free

ingredients.name: ginger
ingredients.note: peeled; grate 2 tbsp for the pot and cut the rest into thin matchsticks to serve

ingredients.name: garam masala
ingredients.note: or swap all the spices for 3 tbsp Shan or National nihari masala, and halve the salt since the packets are salted

ingredients.name: kashmiri chili powder
ingredients.note: at Indian and Pakistani grocers; or 2 tsp paprika

ingredients.name: green chilies
ingredients.note: serrano or Indian green chilies, sliced, to serve

instructions: Heat the oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat and fry the onion, stirring often, for 10 to 12 minutes until deep golden brown. Lift out half onto a paper towel for serving. Don't skip this: the browned onion is the backbone of the gravy.

Lower the heat to medium, add the grated ginger and garlic to the oil left in the pan and stir for 30 seconds. Add the garam masala, fennel, ground ginger, chili powder, cayenne, turmeric and nutmeg and stir for 30 seconds until fragrant; don't let them scorch. Pour in 1 cup of the water and scrape up the bottom.
Put the beef in the slow cooker, sprinkle with the salt and pour the spice mixture and another 2 1/2 cups water over it. The meat shouldn't be fully covered; it releases its own juices as it cooks.
Cover and cook on LOW for 8 to 9 hours or HIGH for 5 to 6 hours, until the meat falls away from the bone and the marrow is soft.

Toast the flour in a dry skillet over medium heat for 2 to 3 minutes until it smells nutty and darkens a shade, then whisk it with the remaining 3/4 cup water until smooth. Turn the slow cooker to HIGH, stir in the slurry and cook covered for 20 to 30 minutes, stirring once, until the gravy is silky and coats a spoon.

Pull out the bones, pushing the marrow into the gravy if you like, and break the meat into big pieces. Taste for salt. A layer of red oil (tari) on top is traditional; spoon some off if you prefer it leaner.
Serve in bowls topped with the fried onion, ginger matchsticks, green chilies, cilantro and a squeeze of lemon, with naan or roti for scooping. Freeze, before garnishing, for up to 3 months.

recipes.title: Slow Cooker Khoresh Fesenjan (Persian Walnut-Pomegranate Chicken)
recipes.summary: Chicken thighs braised in toasted ground walnuts and pomegranate molasses until the sauce turns dark, thick and tangy-sweet. A special-feeling stew that needs almost no work.

ingredients.name: boneless skinless chicken thighs
ingredients.note: left whole; or 3 lb bone-in thighs, skin removed

ingredients.name: pomegranate molasses
ingredients.note: in the Middle Eastern aisle or at Persian and Arab grocers (Cortas, Sadaf); not grenadine

ingredients.name: saffron
ingredients.note: ground and steeped in 2 tbsp hot water

instructions: Toast the walnuts in a dry skillet over medium heat for 5 to 6 minutes, stirring, until fragrant and a shade darker. Cool for a few minutes, then grind in a food processor until fine and clumping like damp sand; stop before it turns to butter. Toasting is where the flavor comes from, so don't skip it.

In the same skillet, heat the oil and cook the onion over medium heat for 8 minutes until soft and golden. Stir in the turmeric and cinnamon for 30 seconds. On a rushed morning you can put the onion and spices in the slow cooker raw; the stew is a little less sweet and deep.

In the slow cooker, whisk the ground walnuts with the water, pomegranate molasses, sugar, salt and pepper, then stir in the onion. Nestle the chicken into the sauce so it's coated. It looks pale and thin now; it darkens and thickens as the walnuts give up their oil.

Cover and cook on LOW for 5 to 6 hours or HIGH for about 3 hours, stirring once halfway if you're home, since the walnuts settle and can catch on the bottom. It's ready when the chicken is very tender, the sauce is deep brown and a sheen of walnut oil sits on top.

Taste and balance: add more pomegranate molasses for sour or more sugar, a teaspoon at a time, for sweet. If it's thinner than gravy, cook uncovered on HIGH for 20 to 30 minutes. Stir in the saffron water if using and break the chicken into large pieces.
Serve over basmati rice, ideally Persian-style with a crisp tahdig, scattered with pomegranate seeds. It's even better the next day and freezes well for 3 months.

recipes.title: Slow Cooker Japanese Chicken Curry (Kare Raisu)
recipes.summary: The mild, glossy curry Japanese kids grow up on: chicken, potatoes, carrots and a grated apple, thickened at the end with a box of curry roux. A dump-and-go weeknight dinner.

ingredients.name: carrots
ingredients.note: large, peeled and cut into 1 1/2-inch chunks

ingredients.name: apple
ingredients.note: small, such as Fuji or Gala, peeled and grated

ingredients.name: japanese curry roux
ingredients.note: 1 box (S&B Golden Curry, House Vermont Curry or Java Curry) in the Asian aisle of most supermarkets; mild for kids, medium or hot for grown-ups

ingredients.name: fukujinzuke
ingredients.note: red pickled vegetables, at Japanese grocers, to serve

instructions: Optional, for a sweeter, deeper curry: cook the onions in the oil in a skillet over medium heat for 8 to 10 minutes until golden. On busy mornings put them in raw; it's still good.

Put the potatoes and carrots in the bottom of the slow cooker, then the onions, garlic, ginger and grated apple, and the chicken on top. Pour in the water; it should come to about the top of the vegetables, not cover the chicken.
Cover and cook on LOW for 6 to 7 hours or HIGH for 3 to 4 hours, until the potatoes are tender when poked with a knife.

Turn the cooker to HIGH. Break the roux into pieces, ladle about 1 cup of the hot cooking liquid into a bowl and whisk the roux in until dissolved, then stir it back into the pot. A slow cooker isn't hot enough to melt the blocks evenly, so this stops lumps. In an Instant Pot, switch to Sauté on low instead.
Stir in the soy sauce, ketchup and honey if using. Cover and cook 15 to 20 minutes, stirring once, until the curry is thick and glossy and coats the back of a spoon.
Serve over short-grain white rice with fukujinzuke on the side. To freeze, scoop out and mash the potatoes into the sauce first (whole chunks go spongy), and keep for up to 3 months.

recipes.title: Slow Cooker Bò Kho (Vietnamese Beef Stew)
recipes.summary: Chunks of beef braised with lemongrass, star anise and coconut water until tender, with sweet carrots and a brick-red broth for dunking baguette. Mild; add chili at the table.

ingredients.name: beef chuck
ingredients.note: cut into 1 1/2- to 2-inch cubes; boneless short rib or shank also work

ingredients.name: fish sauce
ingredients.note: plus more to taste; for gluten-free, check the label has no wheat (Red Boat and Three Crabs are fine)

ingredients.name: five-spice powder
ingredients.note: or 1 packet bò kho spice mix from Vietnamese grocers

ingredients.name: lemongrass
ingredients.note: bottom 6 inches only, bruised with the back of a knife and cut into 3-inch pieces; or 3 tbsp lemongrass paste

ingredients.name: paprika
ingredients.note: for the red color; or use annatto oil, the traditional choice

ingredients.name: coconut water
ingredients.note: unsweetened, not coconut milk; or water plus 1 tsp more sugar

ingredients.name: thai basil
ingredients.note: leaves, to serve; or regular basil

ingredients.name: rice noodles
ingredients.note: cooked, to serve if not using bread

instructions: Toss the beef with the fish sauce, sugar, five-spice, ginger and half the garlic and leave it while you prepare the shallots and lemongrass, or cover and refrigerate overnight so the morning is quicker.

Optional but worth it on a slower morning: heat 1 tbsp oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat and brown the beef in two batches, 3 to 4 minutes each, then tip it into the slow cooker. Browning is for flavor and color; skip it if you're short on time and put the beef straight in.

Heat the remaining oil in the skillet over medium heat. Add the shallots, the rest of the garlic and the lemongrass and stir for 2 minutes, then stir in the tomato paste and paprika for 1 minute until brick red. Splash in a little of the coconut water, scrape up the bottom and pour it all into the slow cooker.
Add the star anise, cinnamon stick and remaining coconut water and pile the carrots on top. The liquid should come about two-thirds of the way up the beef, not cover it.
Cover and cook on LOW for 8 hours or HIGH for 5 hours, until the beef is tender enough to cut with a spoon and the carrots are soft but holding their shape.
Fish out the lemongrass, star anise and cinnamon and skim off the fat. Taste and add more fish sauce or a pinch of sugar. If you like it thicker, cook uncovered on HIGH for 20 to 30 minutes.
Serve in bowls with a crusty baguette for dipping, the way it's eaten for breakfast in Saigon, or over rice noodles or rice. Pass Thai basil, lime and chilies at the table. Freezes well for 3 months.

recipes.title: Slow Cooker Bigos (Polish Hunter's Stew)
recipes.summary: Sauerkraut and fresh cabbage cooked down for hours with pork, kielbasa, dried mushrooms and prunes until tangy, smoky and deep. Better on day two, and it freezes well.

ingredients.name: dried porcini mushrooms
ingredients.note: borowiki at Polish delis, or in the produce section; or 8 oz fresh cremini, sliced

ingredients.name: dry red wine
ingredients.note: many families use it; or more mushroom water

ingredients.name: sauerkraut
ingredients.note: refrigerated bag or jar, Polish brands if you can; drained

ingredients.name: kielbasa
ingredients.note: Polish smoked sausage, sliced into half-moons

ingredients.name: salt
ingredients.note: only if needed at the end

instructions: Cover the dried mushrooms with the hot water and leave to soak while you do everything else.

Cook the bacon in a large skillet over medium heat for 5 minutes until the fat runs. Add the pork and brown it for 6 to 8 minutes; it doesn't need to cook through, this is for flavor. Add the onion for the last 3 minutes, then stir in the tomato paste for 1 minute and pour in the wine if using, scraping up the browned bits. On a rushed morning, put the bacon, pork and onion into the slow cooker raw instead; it's still good bigos.
Taste the sauerkraut: if it's very sharp, rinse it briefly and squeeze it out. Lift the mushrooms from their water, chop them, and pour the soaking water in slowly, leaving the grit behind.

Put the sauerkraut, cabbage, skillet contents, kielbasa, mushrooms and their water, prunes, bay leaves, allspice, marjoram, caraway and pepper in the slow cooker and stir. It will be piled high in a 6-quart cooker, but the cabbage collapses by half within a couple of hours. Don't add more liquid; the cabbage gives plenty.

Cover and cook on LOW for 8 hours or HIGH for 5 hours, until the cabbage is soft and has darkened to a golden brown and the pork falls apart. Stir well; if it's watery, cook uncovered on HIGH for 30 minutes.
Taste and add salt only if it needs it (the kraut, bacon and sausage are salty) and more pepper. Remove the bay leaves.
Serve with rye bread or boiled potatoes. Polish cooks reheat bigos over several days and it gets better each time; it keeps 5 days in the fridge or 3 months frozen.

recipes.title: Fo Tui Tung Fan (Hong Kong Ham Macaroni Soup with Fried Egg)
recipes.summary: The Hong Kong cha chaan teng breakfast: soft macaroni in clear chicken broth with strips of ham and a crisp-edged fried egg on top. Mild, cheap, and on the table in half an hour.

ingredients.name: elbow macaroni
ingredients.note: short straight 'salad' macaroni or ditalini also work

ingredients.name: low-sodium chicken broth
ingredients.note: or 4 cups broth and 2 cups water for a lighter soup

ingredients.name: ham
ingredients.note: sliced deli ham or a ham steak, cut into thin strips; Spam is the other café favorite

ingredients.name: white pepper
ingredients.note: ground; in the spice aisle or at Asian grocers; black pepper also works

ingredients.name: salt
ingredients.note: to taste; the ham and broth are already salty

ingredients.name: frozen corn
ingredients.note: some cafés add corn or peas to the broth

ingredients.name: toasted sesame oil
ingredients.note: a few drops to finish; not every café adds it

instructions: Bring a large pot of water to a boil, add the macaroni and cook 2 to 3 minutes longer than the package says, until very soft; Hong Kong macaroni is tender, not al dente. Drain and rinse briefly under warm water so the starch doesn't cloud the soup.
Meanwhile, bring the broth to a simmer in a second pot with the ham strips (and corn, if using). Simmer 5 minutes so the ham flavors the broth, then season with the white pepper and salt to taste.

Heat the vegetable oil in a nonstick skillet over medium-high until it shimmers. Crack in the eggs and fry 2 to 3 minutes, spooning a little hot oil over the whites, until the edges are brown and lacy and the yolks are still runny. For kids who like a firm yolk, flip and cook about 1 minute more.
Divide the macaroni among 4 deep bowls and ladle the hot broth and ham over it.
Slide an egg onto each bowl, scatter with green onions and add a few drops of sesame oil, if using.
Serve right away, with buttered toast and milk tea or coffee for the full café breakfast. The macaroni keeps soaking up broth as it sits, so don't make it ahead.

recipes.title: Molletes (Bean and Cheese Toasts with Pico de Gallo)
recipes.summary: Split bolillo rolls, buttered and toasted, spread with refried beans and melted cheese, then heaped with fresh pico de gallo. A Mexico City café breakfast that feeds a crowd off one sheet pan.

ingredients.name: bolillo rolls
ingredients.note: from Mexican bakeries and many supermarket bakeries; or crusty French rolls or 6-inch lengths of baguette

ingredients.name: refried beans
ingredients.note: one 16-oz can of refried pinto beans, or homemade; refried black beans are just as common. Many canned 'traditional' refried beans are made with lard, so pick a can labeled vegetarian or vegan

ingredients.name: oaxaca cheese
ingredients.note: shredded or pulled into strands; or Chihuahua, Monterey Jack or low-moisture mozzarella

ingredients.name: serrano pepper
ingredients.note: minced, for the pico; seed it for less heat

instructions: Heat the oven to 400°F. While it heats, make the pico de gallo: stir together the tomatoes, onion, cilantro, serrano (if using), lime juice and salt, and let it sit so the flavors come together.
Split the rolls lengthwise and pull out a little of the soft crumb from each half to make a shallow bed for the beans.
Spread the cut sides with butter and lay them buttered side up on a sheet pan. Bake 5 to 6 minutes, until the edges are golden and crisp.
Meanwhile, warm the beans in a small pan or the microwave with a splash of water until soft and spreadable.

Spread a thick layer of beans over each toasted half and top with the cheese. Bake 5 to 7 minutes more, until the cheese is melted and bubbling at the edges; for browned spots, finish under the broiler for 1 to 2 minutes and watch closely.
Spoon the pico over the hot molletes and serve with pickled jalapeños and your favorite salsa on the side. Add fried eggs to the table for a bigger brunch.

recipes.title: Aloo Paratha (Punjabi Potato-Stuffed Flatbread)
recipes.summary: Whole-wheat flatbreads stuffed with spiced mashed potato and griddled in ghee until golden, served with butter, yogurt and pickle. The classic Punjabi Sunday brunch; mildly hot from green chilies.

ingredients.name: whole wheat flour
ingredients.note: Indian atta (chapati flour), from Indian grocers or the international aisle, makes the softest dough; US whole wheat flour works but is coarser

ingredients.name: water
ingredients.note: lukewarm; start with 3/4 cup and add the rest a tablespoon at a time, since atta and US flours drink different amounts

ingredients.name: salt
ingredients.note: 1/2 tsp for the dough, 1 tsp for the filling

ingredients.name: green chilies
ingredients.note: serrano or Indian green chilies, finely minced; use 1 for mild

ingredients.name: ajwain seeds
ingredients.note: carom seeds, from Indian grocers; or cumin seeds

ingredients.name: amchur
ingredients.note: dried mango powder, from Indian grocers; or 1 tsp lemon juice

ingredients.name: red chili powder
ingredients.note: Kashmiri chili powder for color with little heat; or paprika

ingredients.name: ghee
ingredients.note: melted, for cooking; or vegetable oil

ingredients.name: red onion
ingredients.note: very finely chopped and squeezed dry; some families add it, some never do

ingredients.name: butter
ingredients.note: a pat on each hot paratha, the dhaba way

ingredients.name: mango pickle
ingredients.note: Indian achaar, from Indian grocers, for serving

instructions: Boil the whole, unpeeled potatoes in salted water 20 to 25 minutes, until a knife slides through easily. Drain, peel while warm, then grate on a box grater or mash until completely smooth; lumps tear the dough. Let the potato cool fully, since warm filling makes the dough sticky.

While the potatoes cook, mix the flour with 1/2 tsp salt. Add the water a little at a time and knead 5 to 6 minutes into a soft, smooth dough, softer than pizza dough. Rub with a few drops of ghee, cover and rest at least 20 minutes.

Mix the cooled potato with the chilies, cilantro, ginger, ajwain (crush it between your palms as you add it), amchur, garam masala, chili powder, 1 tsp salt and the onion, if using. Taste: it should be boldly seasoned. Divide into 8 balls.

Divide the dough into 8 balls. Roll one into a 4-inch round, set a ball of filling in the center, bring the edges up and pleat them together over the top, pinch to seal and twist off any extra dough. Flatten gently with your palm.
Dust both sides with flour and roll gently from the center outward into a 7-inch round, turning it often. If filling peeks through, dab on a pinch of flour and keep going.

Heat a cast-iron skillet or tawa over medium-high. Cook a paratha about 45 seconds, until small bubbles appear, flip and cook 30 seconds, then brush the top with ghee, flip and brush the other side. Press the edges with a spatula and cook about 1 minute per side, until crisp golden-brown spots cover both sides.
Stack the cooked parathas in a towel-lined basket to keep warm while you cook the rest. Serve hot with a pat of butter, yogurt and pickle.
To freeze, cook each side just until spotted, without ghee. Cool, stack between squares of parchment and freeze up to 2 months, then cook from frozen with ghee over medium heat.

recipes.title: Ackee and Saltfish
recipes.summary: Jamaica's national dish and Sunday breakfast: flaked salt cod sautéed with onion, sweet peppers, tomato and thyme, then folded with soft, buttery ackee. Mildly hot; soak the fish the night before.

ingredients.name: salt cod
ingredients.note: boneless salted cod (bacalao), in the seafood case or the Caribbean and Latin aisle; Jamaicans call it saltfish

ingredients.name: canned ackee
ingredients.note: a 19-oz can in brine (Grace, Linstead and similar Jamaican brands), drained gently in a colander; from Caribbean grocers or the international aisle. Use canned only: fresh ackee isn't sold in the US, and unripe or unopened ackee is poisonous, so don't swap in fruit picked from a tree

ingredients.name: green onions
ingredients.note: chopped, white and green parts kept separate

ingredients.name: scotch bonnet pepper
ingredients.note: seeded and minced; or a habanero; use a whole one with seeds for real heat

instructions: The night before, cover the saltfish with cold water and soak it in the fridge 8 to 12 hours, changing the water 2 or 3 times. Then put it in a pot of fresh water, bring to a boil and simmer 10 to 15 minutes, until it flakes easily. Short on time: skip the soak, cover with water, boil 15 minutes, drain, and boil 15 minutes more in fresh water.
Taste a flake: it should be pleasantly salty, not harsh; if it's still very salty, boil it again in fresh water for 10 minutes. Drain, cool a little and flake, removing any skin or bones.

Heat the oil in a large skillet over medium. Add the onion, garlic, green onion whites, Scotch bonnet and thyme sprigs and cook 3 to 4 minutes, until the onion softens. Wash your hands after handling the pepper.
Add the bell peppers and tomatoes and cook 3 to 4 minutes, until the peppers are soft and the tomatoes slump.
Stir in the flaked saltfish and black pepper and cook 2 to 3 minutes so the fish picks up the flavors.
Gently fold in the drained ackee and the green onion tops, cover and heat 2 to 3 minutes. Stir as little as possible; ackee is soft and turns to mush if you stir it hard. Pick out the thyme stems.
Serve hot with fried dumplings, boiled green bananas, fried plantain, roast breadfruit or hard dough bread, and a pot of tea.

recipes.title: Kanelbullar i Långpanna (Swedish Cinnamon Bun Bake)
recipes.summary: Cardamom-scented yeast dough rolled with cinnamon butter, sliced and baked close together in one pan, finished with pearl sugar instead of icing. Most of the time is rising; or shape them the night before.

ingredients.name: unsalted butter
ingredients.note: 5 tbsp for the dough, 6 tbsp very soft for the filling

ingredients.name: all-purpose flour
ingredients.note: spooned and leveled, plus more for rolling

ingredients.name: granulated sugar
ingredients.note: 1/4 cup for the dough, 1/2 cup for the filling

ingredients.name: instant yeast
ingredients.note: one packet; for active dry, stir it into the warm milk and wait 5 minutes until foamy

ingredients.name: ground cardamom
ingredients.note: 1 1/2 tsp for the dough, 1/2 tsp for the filling; freshly crushed seeds from green pods taste best, and Indian grocers sell them cheaply

ingredients.name: egg
ingredients.note: beaten with 1 tbsp water, for brushing

ingredients.name: pearl sugar
ingredients.note: Swedish pärlsocker, at IKEA or online; or coarsely crushed sugar cubes or turbinado sugar

instructions: Warm the milk with 5 tbsp butter until the butter melts, then let it cool to lukewarm, about 105°F (comfortable on your wrist). In a large bowl, whisk the flour, 1/4 cup sugar, yeast, 1 1/2 tsp cardamom and the salt. Add the milk mixture and stir into a soft dough.
Knead 8 to 10 minutes by hand, or 6 minutes in a stand mixer with the dough hook, until smooth, elastic and only slightly tacky. Cover and let rise somewhere warm for 1 to 1 1/2 hours, until doubled.
Meanwhile, beat the 6 tbsp very soft butter with 1/2 cup sugar, the cinnamon and the remaining 1/2 tsp cardamom into a spreadable paste. Butter a 9x13-inch pan.

Roll the dough on a lightly floured counter into a rectangle about 12 by 20 inches. Spread the filling right to the edges, roll it up tightly from a long side and pinch the seam closed. Cut into 15 slices with a sharp knife or unflavored dental floss.

Arrange the slices cut side up in the pan, 3 by 5. Cover and let rise about 45 minutes, until puffy and touching. To make ahead, cover and refrigerate the shaped buns overnight instead, then set them on the counter for 45 to 60 minutes while the oven heats.
Heat the oven to 375°F. Brush the buns with the egg wash and scatter with pearl sugar. Bake 22 to 25 minutes, until deep golden and the center bun reads 190°F; tent with foil if they brown too fast.
Cool 10 minutes in the pan, then pull apart and serve warm with coffee for fika. Leftovers freeze well for a month; rewarm them wrapped in foil at 325°F for about 10 minutes.

recipes.title: Buttermilk Biscuits and Sausage Gravy
recipes.summary: Tall, flaky buttermilk biscuits split open and smothered in peppery cream gravy made with browned breakfast sausage. The Southern Sunday breakfast that fills up a whole table.

ingredients.name: all-purpose flour
ingredients.note: 3 cups for the biscuits, 1/4 cup for the gravy; a Southern soft-wheat flour like White Lily makes the most tender biscuits

ingredients.name: salt
ingredients.note: 1 tsp for the biscuits, the rest to taste in the gravy

ingredients.name: unsalted butter
ingredients.note: 8 tbsp very cold and cubed (or frozen and grated) for the biscuits, 2 tbsp melted for brushing

ingredients.name: buttermilk
ingredients.note: cold; or 1 1/4 cups milk with 1 tbsp lemon juice, rested 5 minutes

ingredients.name: pork breakfast sausage
ingredients.note: bulk (not links), regular or sage; hot breakfast sausage if you like a kick

ingredients.name: whole milk
ingredients.note: plus a splash to loosen the gravy

ingredients.name: black pepper
ingredients.note: coarsely ground; the gravy should be speckled

instructions: Heat the oven to 450°F and line a sheet pan with parchment. Whisk 3 cups flour with the baking powder, baking soda and 1 tsp salt.

Cut the 8 tbsp cold butter into the flour with a pastry cutter or your fingertips until the pieces are the size of peas. Stir in the cold buttermilk with a fork just until a shaggy dough forms; a few dry bits are fine.

Turn the dough onto a floured counter, pat it into a rectangle about 1 inch thick and fold it in thirds like a letter. Pat out and fold twice more for flaky layers, then pat to 1 inch thick. Cut 2 1/2-inch rounds, pressing straight down without twisting, and press the scraps together once for a few more.
Set the biscuits on the pan with their sides touching so they rise tall. Bake 13 to 16 minutes, until risen and golden brown on top, then brush with the melted butter.

While the biscuits bake, brown the sausage in a large skillet over medium-high, breaking it into small crumbles, 7 to 8 minutes, until no pink remains. Don't drain it: you want about 3 tbsp of fat in the pan. If the sausage is lean, add a tablespoon of butter.

Sprinkle 1/4 cup flour over the sausage and stir 1 to 2 minutes to cook out the raw taste. Slowly pour in the milk while stirring, bring to a simmer and cook 4 to 6 minutes, stirring often, until the gravy thickly coats a spoon. It thickens more as it stands; loosen it with a splash of milk.
Season generously with black pepper, salt to taste and the cayenne, if using. Split the warm biscuits, ladle the gravy over and serve right away.

recipes.title: Steak au Poivre for Two with Roasted Baby Potatoes
recipes.summary: Peppercorn-crusted strip steaks seared in a hot skillet, with a quick cognac and cream pan sauce made in the same pan. Bistro dinner at home; the pepper is warm, not fiery.

ingredients.name: new york strip steaks
ingredients.note: about 10 oz each and 1 to 1 1/4 inches thick; or two 7 oz filet mignon steaks, the classic cut

ingredients.name: cognac
ingredients.note: or any brandy; for no alcohol, use 1/3 cup more broth and 1 tsp sherry vinegar

ingredients.name: dijon mustard
ingredients.note: some bistros add it, some don't

instructions: Heat the oven to 425°F. Toss the potatoes with the olive oil, 1/2 tsp salt and the thyme sprigs on a small sheet pan and turn them cut side down. Roast 30 to 35 minutes, until the cut sides are deep golden and a knife slides in easily.
