While they roast, pat the steaks very dry and salt them on both sides with the remaining 1 tsp salt. Put the peppercorns in a zip-top bag and crack them with the bottom of a heavy pan into coarse pieces; you want cracked pepper, not powder. Press the pepper firmly onto both sides of each steak so it sticks.

When the potatoes have about 15 minutes left, heat the vegetable oil in a heavy skillet (cast iron or stainless, not nonstick) over medium-high until it shimmers. Lay in the steaks and leave them alone for 4 minutes, until a dark crust forms.

Flip, add 1 tbsp butter and cook 3 to 4 minutes more, spooning the butter over, until the thickest part reads 125°F for medium-rare (130°F for medium). Move the steaks to a plate and rest them loosely covered for 5 to 8 minutes.

Pour off all but about 1 tbsp fat and turn the heat to medium. Add the shallot and stir for 1 minute until soft. Take the pan off the heat, add the cognac (stand back; it can flare), then return it to the heat and let it bubble, scraping up the browned bits, until almost gone, about 1 minute.

Add the broth and boil until reduced by half, about 2 minutes. Stir in the cream, the mustard if using and any juices from the resting plate, and simmer until the sauce coats a spoon, 2 to 3 minutes. Off the heat, swirl in the last 1 tbsp butter and taste for salt.
Serve the steaks whole or sliced against the grain with the sauce spooned over, the potatoes alongside and a little parsley on top.

recipes.title: Thai Green Curry Mussels with Thai Basil
recipes.summary: Mussels steamed open in green curry coconut sauce with makrut lime leaves and Thai basil, with jasmine rice for the sauce. Medium-hot; use less paste for milder.

ingredients.name: mussels
ingredients.note: live, in the shell; most supermarket seafood counters sell them cleaned in 2 lb bags

ingredients.name: coconut milk
ingredients.note: 13.5 oz, full-fat, such as Chaokoh or Aroy-D; don't shake the can

ingredients.name: green curry paste
ingredients.note: Maesri or Mae Ploy (Asian grocers) are hot; with Thai Kitchen (supermarkets) use 3 tbsp. Most are gluten-free; check the label

ingredients.name: makrut lime leaves
ingredients.note: torn, center rib removed; frozen at Asian grocers. Or 1 tsp grated lime zest

ingredients.name: fish sauce
ingredients.note: plus more to taste; most brands are gluten-free, but a few add wheat protein, so check the label

ingredients.name: thai basil
ingredients.note: leaves, loosely packed; or Italian basil

ingredients.name: red chili
ingredients.note: Fresno or red Thai chili, thinly sliced, for more heat and color

instructions: Rinse the rice in a few changes of water until it runs mostly clear. Put it in a small pot with the 1 1/4 cups water and a pinch of salt, bring to a boil, then cover and cook on the lowest heat for 15 minutes. Turn off the heat and leave it covered for 10 minutes.

Meanwhile, clean the mussels: rinse them in cold water and pull off any stringy beards, tugging toward the hinge. Tap any open ones sharply on the counter; throw away any that don't close, and any with cracked shells. Keep them in the fridge until you cook.

Spoon about 1/2 cup of the thick cream off the top of the unshaken coconut milk into a wide pot with a lid. Add the oil and cook over medium, stirring, for 3 to 4 minutes, until it bubbles thickly and little pools of oil start to separate. Some US brands have stabilizers and never split; if yours just bubbles, carry on after 4 minutes.

Add the curry paste and fry it in the coconut cream for about 2 minutes, stirring constantly, until it smells strongly fragrant and the oil turns green. Frying the paste this way is what gives the sauce its depth.

Pour in the rest of the coconut milk and add the lime leaves, fish sauce and palm sugar. Simmer 3 minutes, then taste: it should be a little sweet and hot, and slightly under-salted, because the mussels release salty juices as they open.
Turn the heat to medium-high, tip in the mussels, stir to coat and cover tightly. Cook 4 to 6 minutes, shaking the pot once, until the shells have opened wide. Throw away any that stay shut.

Turn off the heat and stir in the basil and the chili if using. Taste the sauce and add a splash more fish sauce only if it needs it. Ladle the mussels and plenty of sauce into wide bowls, squeeze over a lime wedge, and serve the rice alongside with an empty bowl for shells.

recipes.title: Risotto alla Zucca (Butternut Squash and Sage Risotto)
recipes.summary: A northern Italian autumn risotto: butternut squash cooked down into the rice until it turns creamy and golden, finished with butter, Parmesan and crisp fried sage.

ingredients.name: vegetable broth
ingredients.note: low-sodium; you may not need it all

ingredients.name: unsalted butter
ingredients.note: divided; keep 2 tbsp cold and cubed for the end

ingredients.name: shallot
ingredients.note: large, finely chopped; or 1/2 small yellow onion

ingredients.name: butternut squash
ingredients.note: peeled, seeded and cut into 1/2-inch cubes (about 2 1/2 cups); pre-cut squash works

ingredients.name: dry white wine
ingredients.note: such as pinot grigio; or skip it and add 2 tsp lemon juice at the end

ingredients.name: parmesan cheese
ingredients.note: finely grated, plus more to serve; Parmigiano-Reggiano uses animal rennet, so pick a vegetarian hard cheese if that matters to you

instructions: Bring the broth to a bare simmer in a saucepan and keep it hot over low heat. Cold broth stalls the rice.

In a wide, heavy pan, melt 1 tbsp butter with the olive oil over medium heat. Fry the sage leaves for 30 to 60 seconds until they darken slightly and stop bubbling, then lift them onto a paper towel and sprinkle with a little salt. Leave the fat in the pan.

Add the shallot and a pinch of salt and cook 3 minutes until soft but not browned. Add the squash and cook 5 minutes, stirring now and then. Add a ladle of broth, cover and cook another 5 minutes, until the squash is soft at the edges.
Uncover and let any liquid left in the pan cook off for a minute. Add the rice and stir for 2 minutes until the grains look glassy at the edges. Pour in the wine and stir until it's absorbed.

Add a ladle (about 1/2 cup) of hot broth and stir often until the pan is nearly dry, then add the next. Keep going for 18 to 20 minutes. Press some squash cubes against the side of the pan as you go so they melt into the rice. It's ready when the rice is tender with a slight bite in the center and the risotto slowly spreads when you shake the pan.

Take the pan off the heat. Add the 2 tbsp cold butter and the Parmesan and beat hard with a wooden spoon for 30 seconds until glossy and creamy; add a splash more broth if it's stiff. Cover and let it sit 1 to 2 minutes. Season with salt, pepper and the nutmeg if using.
Spoon into warm shallow bowls, crumble the fried sage over the top and pass more Parmesan.

recipes.title: Molten Chocolate Lava Cakes for Two
recipes.summary: Two small chocolate cakes baked in ramekins until set outside and still runny in the middle. You can fill the ramekins hours ahead and bake them while you clear the plates.

ingredients.name: bittersweet chocolate
ingredients.note: 60 to 70% cacao bar, chopped; chocolate chips don't melt as smoothly

ingredients.name: egg
ingredients.note: large, at room temperature; the center stays runny, so use pasteurized eggs if serving anyone pregnant, very young, older or with a weakened immune system

ingredients.name: vanilla ice cream
ingredients.note: about 2 scoops; or whipped cream or raspberries, to serve

instructions: Heat the oven to 425°F with a rack in the middle. Butter two 6 oz ramekins well, add the cocoa powder and tilt and tap to coat the insides, then tip out the extra. Put them on a small baking sheet.
Melt the chocolate and butter together in a heatproof bowl set over a pan of barely simmering water, or in the microwave in 20-second bursts, stirring until smooth. Let it cool for a few minutes.
In another bowl, whisk the egg, egg yolk, sugar, salt and vanilla for about 2 minutes, until pale and slightly thickened.

Fold the chocolate into the eggs, then sift or sprinkle the flour over and fold until no streaks remain. Divide between the ramekins; they'll be about two-thirds full. (You can cover and refrigerate them now for up to a day; bake straight from the fridge and add about 2 minutes.)

Bake 10 to 12 minutes, until the tops are puffed and look dry and the edges are firm and just pulling away from the sides, but the very center still jiggles slightly when you nudge the pan. Ovens vary, so check at 10 minutes the first time; a minute too long and the middle sets.

Let them stand 1 to 2 minutes. Holding each ramekin with an oven mitt, run a thin knife around the edge, put a dessert plate on top and flip, then wait a few seconds and lift off the ramekin. Dust with powdered sugar and serve right away with ice cream or berries.

recipes.title: Sake no Kamizutsumi-yaki (Salmon and Mushrooms Baked in Parchment)
recipes.summary: Salmon, mushrooms and onion sealed in parchment with butter, sake and soy sauce, then opened at the table in a puff of steam. The juices are for spooning over rice.

ingredients.name: short-grain rice
ingredients.note: Japanese-style, such as Calrose or Nishiki

ingredients.name: salmon fillets
ingredients.note: about 6 oz each and 1 inch thick, skin on or off

ingredients.name: sake
ingredients.note: divided; dry cooking sake or drinking sake, from Asian grocers or liquor stores. Or dry white wine; for no alcohol, use water

ingredients.name: shimeji mushrooms
ingredients.note: 1 pack, base trimmed and pulled apart; or enoki, or sliced cremini

ingredients.name: lemon
ingredients.note: 2 thin slices, the rest in wedges

instructions: Rinse the rice in a bowl of cold water, swishing and draining 3 or 4 times until the water is nearly clear. Soak it in the 1 1/4 cups water for 30 minutes if you have time, then bring to a boil, cover and cook on the lowest heat for 13 minutes. Turn off the heat and leave it covered for 10 minutes.
Sprinkle the salmon on both sides with the salt and 1 tbsp sake and let it sit 10 minutes. Pat it dry with paper towels; this firms the flesh and takes away any fishy smell.

Heat the oven to 400°F. Tear two 15-inch sheets of parchment, fold each in half and open it up again. Pile half the onion just to one side of each fold, set a salmon fillet on top, and tuck the mushrooms around and over it.
Dot the butter over the fish, lay a lemon slice on each fillet, and drizzle each with 1 tbsp sake and 1 tsp soy sauce.
Fold the paper over and seal the open edges with small, tight, overlapping folds all the way around, so no steam escapes. Put the packets on a sheet pan.

Bake 14 to 16 minutes, until the packets puff. To check, open one corner carefully: the salmon is done when it is opaque at the edges and just flakes at the thickest part (125 to 130°F on a thermometer). Fold it closed again.

Put each packet on a plate and cut it open at the table, watching for steam. Top with green onion and shichimi if you like, and serve with the rice, lemon wedges and the buttery juices spooned over everything.

recipes.title: Shishlik (Persian Saffron Lamb Chops) with Kateh Rice
recipes.summary: Lamb rib chops marinated in grated onion, saffron and lemon, seared hard in a grill pan, with blistered tomatoes and buttery Persian pot rice. The marinade needs 4 hours or overnight.

ingredients.name: lamb rib chops
ingredients.note: about 8 chops, frenched if you like; or 4 lamb loin chops

ingredients.name: onion
ingredients.note: medium, grated on the large holes of a box grater

ingredients.name: saffron threads
ingredients.note: loosely packed; ground with a pinch of sugar

ingredients.name: sumac
ingredients.note: for sprinkling; at Middle Eastern grocers or the spice aisle

ingredients.name: fresh herbs
ingredients.note: mint, basil and tarragon sprigs with a few radishes, to eat alongside (sabzi khordan)

instructions: Grind the saffron with a pinch of sugar in a mortar (or crush it between two spoons) and pour 3 tbsp hot water over it. Let it steep 10 minutes until deep orange.

In a bowl or zip-top bag, mix the grated onion and its juice, half the saffron water, the lemon juice, olive oil and pepper. Add the chops and turn to coat. Cover and refrigerate at least 4 hours or overnight; don't add salt yet.

For the kateh, rinse the rice in several changes of water until it runs clear. Put it in a small nonstick pot with the 1 3/4 cups water, 1 tsp salt and 1 tbsp butter, bring to a boil and cook uncovered over medium until the water is absorbed and little holes appear on the surface, about 10 minutes.

Turn the heat to low, wrap the lid in a clean kitchen towel, cover tightly and steam 25 to 30 minutes. The bottom will form a golden crust. Meanwhile, melt the other 1 tbsp butter into the remaining saffron water for basting.

About 15 minutes before the rice is done, scrape most of the onion off the chops, pat them fairly dry and season with the remaining 1 tsp salt. Heat a grill pan or cast-iron skillet over high until it smokes lightly. Sear the tomatoes cut side down for 3 to 4 minutes until blistered, then set them aside.

Sear the chops 2 to 3 minutes per side, brushing with the saffron butter after you flip, until well browned and 130°F inside for medium-rare. Work in two batches if the pan is crowded. Rest 3 minutes.
Fluff the rice onto plates and break the crust into pieces alongside. Add the chops and tomatoes, brush with any remaining saffron butter, sprinkle with sumac and serve with the herbs.

recipes.title: Arroz Caldo (Filipino Chicken and Ginger Rice Porridge)
recipes.summary: Rice simmered with chicken, plenty of ginger and fish sauce into a thick, savory porridge, topped with golden garlic and scallions. The bowl Filipino families make when someone feels rough.

ingredients.name: chicken thighs
ingredients.note: boneless, skinless, cut into bite-size pieces

ingredients.name: garlic
ingredients.note: 4 minced for the pot, 4 thinly sliced for the topping

ingredients.name: ginger
ingredients.note: peeled and cut into thin matchsticks

ingredients.name: fish sauce
ingredients.note: patis; in the Asian aisle of most supermarkets

ingredients.name: jasmine rice
ingredients.note: rinsed; many cooks swap 1/4 cup of it for glutinous (sweet) rice from Asian grocers for a silkier porridge

ingredients.name: calamansi
ingredients.note: halved; sold frozen at Filipino and Asian grocers, or use lemon wedges

instructions: Heat the oil in a large heavy pot over medium-low heat. Add the sliced garlic and cook, stirring, 3 to 4 minutes until pale golden, then lift it out onto a paper towel; it crisps as it cools. Leave the oil in the pot.
Raise the heat to medium. Add the onion, minced garlic and ginger and cook 3 to 4 minutes until the onion is soft and the ginger smells sweet.
Add the chicken and cook, turning, 4 to 5 minutes until no longer pink on the outside. Stir in the fish sauce and cook 1 minute more.
Add the rinsed rice and stir for 1 to 2 minutes so every grain is coated.

Pour in 6 cups of the broth and bring to a boil, then lower to a gentle simmer and partly cover. Cook 30 to 35 minutes, stirring and scraping the bottom every 5 minutes, until the grains have burst and the porridge is thick and creamy. Add the rest of the broth as it thickens; it should slide slowly off a spoon.
Taste and add more fish sauce and black pepper if it needs it. Ladle into bowls and top with the crisp garlic, green onions, egg halves and a squeeze of calamansi.
It thickens a lot as it stands, so loosen leftovers with a splash of broth or water when you reheat them.

recipes.title: Hobakjuk (Korean Pumpkin Porridge)
recipes.summary: A silky, lightly sweet porridge of kabocha squash thickened with sweet rice flour. Korean families serve it warm for breakfast or to anyone who wants something soft and gentle.

ingredients.name: kabocha squash
ingredients.note: 1 small squash; sold as Japanese pumpkin in most supermarkets, or use butternut squash

ingredients.name: sweet rice flour
ingredients.note: glutinous rice flour such as Mochiko, in the baking or Asian aisle; regular rice flour works but is less silky

ingredients.name: sugar
ingredients.note: add more or less to taste

ingredients.name: canned sweet red beans
ingredients.note: pat (adzuki); at Korean and Asian grocers

instructions: Microwave the whole squash for 3 to 4 minutes to soften the skin. Halve it, scoop out the seeds, cut it into wedges, peel with a sharp knife or sturdy peeler and cut the flesh into 1-inch chunks.
Put the squash in a pot with 3 1/2 cups of the water and bring to a boil. Cover and simmer over medium-low heat 15 to 20 minutes, until a fork slides through a chunk with no resistance.
Blend until smooth with an immersion blender in the pot, or in batches in a blender with the lid vented. A few small lumps are fine; some families like them.
Whisk the sweet rice flour with the remaining 1/2 cup cold water in a small bowl until no lumps remain.

Bring the squash back to a gentle simmer and drizzle in the slurry, stirring all the time. Cook 5 to 7 minutes, stirring often with a long spoon because it bubbles and spits, until it coats the back of the spoon and no longer tastes floury.
Stir in the sugar and salt and taste: it should be lightly sweet, with the salt bringing out the squash. Warm the red beans in it if using, then ladle into bowls and scatter with pine nuts.

recipes.title: Caldo de Pollo (Mexican Chicken and Vegetable Soup)
recipes.summary: Bone-in chicken simmered with big pieces of carrot, potato, zucchini and corn into a clear, gentle broth. Served with rice, lime and warm tortillas, it's Sunday lunch and sick-day dinner in many Mexican homes.

ingredients.name: bone-in chicken pieces
ingredients.note: drumsticks and thighs; skin removed for a clearer, lighter broth

ingredients.name: cilantro
ingredients.note: a few sprigs for the pot, the rest chopped for serving

ingredients.name: potatoes
ingredients.note: Yukon Gold or red, cut into large chunks

ingredients.name: zucchini
ingredients.note: cut into thick rounds; Mexican gray squash if you see it

ingredients.name: chicken bouillon powder
ingredients.note: the Knorr-style powder many Mexican kitchens keep; check the label if you need it gluten-free, or use more salt

ingredients.name: cooked rice
ingredients.note: white or arroz rojo, a spoonful in each bowl

instructions: Put the chicken, water, onion, garlic, celery, a few cilantro sprigs and the salt in a large pot (at least 8 quarts). Bring to a boil over high heat, skimming off the gray foam for the first few minutes so the broth stays clear.
Lower the heat to a gentle simmer, partly cover and cook 25 minutes.
Add the carrots and corn and simmer 10 minutes.

Add the potatoes and simmer 10 minutes, then add the zucchini and simmer 8 to 10 minutes more, until a knife slides easily into the potatoes, the zucchini is just soft and the chicken pulls away from the bone.
Fish out the onion, celery and cilantro sprigs. Taste the broth and add bouillon powder or more salt until it tastes rich.
Put a piece of chicken and some of each vegetable in each bowl, ladle the broth over and add a spoonful of rice, chopped cilantro and a squeeze of lime. Serve with warm tortillas.
For a small child or someone with little appetite, pull the chicken off the bone and cut the vegetables into spoon-size pieces before serving.

recipes.title: Kakitama Udon (Japanese Egg Drop Udon)
recipes.summary: Chewy udon in a hot, lightly thickened dashi broth with soft ribbons of egg and a little fresh ginger. Quick, mild and easy to slurp when you don't feel like eating much.

ingredients.name: dried udon noodles
ingredients.note: or 2 blocks of frozen udon from the freezer case at Asian grocers, which need only a minute

ingredients.name: water
ingredients.note: for the broth, plus more for the noodles

ingredients.name: dashi powder
ingredients.note: instant dashi granules such as Hondashi, in the Asian aisle; made with bonito (fish)

ingredients.name: soy sauce
ingredients.note: usukuchi (light-colored) soy keeps the broth pale; regular is fine

ingredients.name: sugar
ingredients.note: stands in for the mirin many cooks use, so the broth has no alcohol

ingredients.name: cornstarch
ingredients.note: or potato starch (katakuriko), stirred into 2 tbsp cold water

instructions: Cook the udon in a pot of boiling water as the package says (8 to 10 minutes for dried, about 1 minute for frozen) until chewy-tender. Drain, rinse briefly under hot water and divide between two deep bowls.
Meanwhile, bring 2 1/2 cups water, the dashi powder, soy sauce and sugar to a simmer in a medium saucepan. Taste: it should be savory with a faint sweetness.
Stir the cornstarch slurry and pour it into the simmering broth, stirring. Cook about 1 minute until the broth turns glossy and slightly thick.

Keep the broth at a steady simmer and stir it in a slow circle. Pour the beaten egg in a thin stream, through the tines of a fork if you have one, then leave it for 20 to 30 seconds until it sets into soft clouds. Stir once gently and turn off the heat.
Ladle the egg broth over the noodles, top with green onions and grated ginger, and eat right away while it's hot.

recipes.title: Yayla Çorbası (Turkish Yogurt and Rice Soup)
recipes.summary: A creamy, gently tangy soup of yogurt and soft rice, finished with butter sizzled with dried mint. Turkish families make it for anyone feeling poorly, and it's ready in about 40 minutes.

ingredients.name: short-grain rice
ingredients.note: rinsed; baldo or calrose, or arborio

ingredients.name: vegetable broth
ingredients.note: or chicken broth, as many Turkish cooks use; plain water works too

ingredients.name: plain whole-milk yogurt
ingredients.note: Turkish, Greek or regular plain yogurt; thin thick Greek yogurt with a splash of water

ingredients.name: dried mint
ingredients.note: at Middle Eastern grocers or in the spice aisle; or the leaves from a pure spearmint tea bag

instructions: Put the rice and broth in a medium pot, bring to a boil, then lower the heat and simmer 15 to 18 minutes until the rice is very soft.
Meanwhile, whisk the yogurt, egg yolk and flour in a bowl until completely smooth; any lumps now stay lumps once it's hot.
Whisking all the time, add a ladle of the hot broth to the yogurt, then another, until the mixture is warm and loose.

Turn the heat under the pot to low and pour in the yogurt slowly, stirring. Keep stirring in one direction, as Turkish cooks do, and raise the heat to medium. Cook 5 to 7 minutes until it barely bubbles and turns smooth and creamy; don't let it boil hard or the yogurt can split. Season with salt.
Melt the butter in a small pan over medium heat until foaming, take it off the heat and stir in the dried mint. It sizzles and smells like fresh mint tea.
Ladle the soup into bowls and drizzle with the mint butter. It thickens as it stands, so loosen leftovers with a little broth or water and reheat gently.

recipes.title: Zheng Shui Dan (Chinese Steamed Egg Custard)
recipes.summary: Eggs whisked with warm water and steamed into a trembling, silky custard, finished with a few drops of soy sauce and sesame oil. A Cantonese home staple to spoon over rice.

ingredients.name: water
ingredients.note: warm, not hot; or low-sodium chicken broth for a richer custard

instructions: Beat the eggs with the salt until fully combined but not foamy, then stir in the warm water.
Pour through a fine sieve into a shallow heatproof bowl that holds about 1 quart. Pop or skim off any bubbles on the surface and cover the bowl with a heatproof plate or foil.
Set a rack in a wok or wide pot with about 1 inch of water and bring it to a boil. Set the bowl on the rack, cover the pot and lower the heat to medium-low so the water just simmers.

Steam 10 to 12 minutes, until the edges are set and the center wobbles like soft tofu when you nudge the bowl; a toothpick in the middle should come out with no runny egg. Low, steady heat keeps the top smooth instead of pitted.
Drizzle the soy sauce and sesame oil over the top and scatter with green onion. Serve warm with steamed rice.

recipes.title: Thayir Sadam (South Indian Curd Rice)
recipes.summary: Soft rice mashed with yogurt and a little milk, finished with a sizzle of mustard seeds, curry leaves and ginger. The mild, creamy close to a South Indian meal, and a bowl many families turn to on an off day.

ingredients.name: white rice
ingredients.note: sona masoori or ponni from Indian grocers, or any medium-grain rice; basmati works

ingredients.name: water
ingredients.note: the extra water makes the very soft rice this needs

ingredients.name: plain whole-milk yogurt
ingredients.note: plain, not Greek; homemade dahi is traditional

ingredients.name: milk
ingredients.note: keeps it mild as it sits

ingredients.name: black mustard seeds
ingredients.note: at Indian grocers; brown mustard seeds work

ingredients.name: curry leaves
ingredients.note: fresh, from Indian grocers; skip if you can't find them

ingredients.name: urad dal
ingredients.note: split white lentils, for crunch in the tempering

ingredients.name: asafoetida
ingredients.note: hing; many brands contain wheat, so pick a gluten-free one

instructions: Rinse the rice and bring it to a boil with the 3 cups water and a pinch of the salt, then cover and cook over low heat 18 to 20 minutes until very soft and the water is absorbed. Mash it with the back of a ladle while hot.
Let the rice cool until just warm, about 10 minutes; yogurt stirred into very hot rice turns sour and grainy.
Stir in the milk, then the yogurt and remaining salt, until creamy and loose like a thick porridge. Add a splash more milk or water if it's stiff.

Heat the ghee in a small pan over medium heat and add the mustard seeds. When they start to pop, after about 30 seconds, add the urad dal if using and stir until golden, then add the ginger, curry leaves and asafoetida. Take the pan off the heat after 10 seconds of crackling.
Pour the tempering over the rice and stir it through. Serve at room temperature or just warm, with pomegranate seeds on top.

recipes.title: Mannaya Kasha (Semolina Milk Porridge)
recipes.summary: Fine semolina whisked into simmering milk for a smooth, lightly sweet porridge with butter melting on top. Ready in about ten minutes; the breakfast many Russian, Ukrainian and Polish families grew up on.

ingredients.name: whole milk
ingredients.note: or half milk, half water for a lighter porridge

ingredients.name: semolina flour
ingredients.note: fine semolina (manka) from Russian or Polish delis; farina such as Cream of Wheat is the closest supermarket match. Coarse yellow durum semolina works but is grittier

ingredients.name: berry jam
ingredients.note: or a drizzle of honey or a few berries

instructions: Bring the milk, sugar and salt to a simmer in a small heavy saucepan over medium heat, watching closely so it doesn't boil over.
Whisking constantly, pour in the semolina in a thin, slow stream; this is what keeps it smooth and lump-free.

Lower the heat and keep stirring 3 to 5 minutes, until it thickens to a loose porridge that coats the spoon. It firms up as it cools, so take it off the heat while it's a little thinner than you want.
Cover and let it stand 2 minutes. Spoon into bowls and top each with half the butter and a spoonful of jam.

recipes.title: Gaeng Jued Tao Hoo (Thai Clear Soup with Tofu and Pork)
recipes.summary: A light, clear broth with tender little pork meatballs, soft tofu and napa cabbage, seasoned with garlic, cilantro and white pepper. The mild everyday Thai soup families eat with rice, with no chili at all.

ingredients.name: cilantro
ingredients.note: stems (and roots, if attached) for the paste, leaves to finish; Asian grocers often sell it with roots on

ingredients.name: white pepper
ingredients.note: ground, from the spice aisle; black pepper works but tastes sharper

ingredients.name: silken tofu
ingredients.note: soft or silken; Thai cooks often use egg tofu tubes from Asian grocers

ingredients.name: glass noodles
ingredients.note: woon sen (mung bean vermicelli), soaked 10 minutes in warm water and cut shorter

instructions: Finely chop about 2 tablespoons of cilantro stems and roots. Pound them with the garlic and white pepper in a mortar, or chop everything together on a board, to a rough paste.
In a bowl, mix the pork with half the paste and 1 tablespoon of the fish sauce, then knead with your hand for a minute until sticky.
Bring the broth and the remaining paste to a boil in a pot and simmer 2 to 3 minutes until fragrant.
With wet hands, pinch off teaspoon-size pieces of pork and drop them into the simmering broth. Cook 4 to 5 minutes until they float and are no longer pink inside, skimming off any foam.
Add the napa cabbage, and the soaked glass noodles if using, and simmer 3 to 4 minutes until the cabbage stems are tender.
Cut the tofu into 1-inch cubes and slide them in gently. Simmer 2 minutes just to heat through, without stirring hard so the tofu stays whole. Season with the remaining fish sauce to taste.
Ladle into bowls, scatter with cilantro leaves and serve hot with steamed jasmine rice.

recipes.title: Changua (Colombian Milk and Egg Breakfast Soup)
recipes.summary: A Bogotá breakfast of eggs poached in a milky scallion broth, ladled over toasted bread and finished with cilantro. Warm, mild and ready in about twenty minutes.

ingredients.name: green onions
ingredients.note: white and light green parts finely chopped, plus some sliced greens to finish

ingredients.name: bread
ingredients.note: day-old, toasted and torn; calado (Colombian dry bread) from Latin grocers is traditional, or use plain croutons

ingredients.name: queso fresco
ingredients.note: crumbled; a few cubes in each bowl, as many Bogotá families do

instructions: Put the milk, water, chopped green onion and salt in a wide saucepan over medium heat. Bring to a gentle simmer, with small bubbles at the edges, about 6 to 8 minutes; watch it, because milk boils over fast. Let it simmer 3 minutes more so the green onion flavors the broth.
Meanwhile, divide the toasted bread among 4 bowls.
Crack each egg into a small cup. Turn the heat down so the liquid just trembles and slide the eggs in one at a time, spaced apart.
Poach 3 to 4 minutes, spooning hot milk over the tops, until the whites are set and the yolks still soft. Give them 5 minutes for firm yolks, which suit little kids.
Ladle an egg and plenty of broth over the bread in each bowl. Top with cilantro, green onion greens and queso fresco if using, and eat right away while the bread still has some bite.
